İspanya'da bir mahkeme, iki eski çalışanının cinsel istismar suçlamasıyla şikâyette bulunmasının ardından ünlü şarkıcı Julio Iglesias hakkında çarşamba günü soruşturma başlattı. Iglesias ise hakkındaki suçlamaları reddediyor.
Madrid Ulusal Mahkemesi (Audiencia Nacional), yaptığı açıklamada, cinsel saldırının yanı sıra fiziksel zarar verme ve aşağılayıcı muamele gibi çeşitli suçları kapsayan "cinsel özgürlüğe karşı suçlar" kapsamında soruşturma yürütüleceğini bildirdi.
Karar, daha önce yapılan bir şikâyetin, iddia edilen suçların Bahamalar ve Dominik Cumhuriyeti'nde işlendiği ve İspanyol mahkemelerinin bu konuda yargı yetkisi bulunmadığı gerekçesiyle reddedilmesinin ardından geldi.
Ev işlerinde çalışan bir kadın ile fizyoterapist olan iki eski çalışan, 2021 yılında Karayipler'deki söz konusu iki ülkede Iglesias'a ait mülklerde çalıştıkları sırada cinsel istismara ve farklı türlerde kötü muameleye maruz kaldıklarını öne sürüyor.
İlk şikâyetin reddedilmesinin ardından Women’s Link Worldwide adlı kuruluş, geçen eylül ayında şarkıcı hakkında doğrudan İspanya Ulusal Mahkemesi'ne suç duyurusunda bulunacağını açıklamıştı.
Kuruluş, Iglesias'ı zorla çalıştırma ve kölelik amacıyla insan ticareti, cinsel özgürlüğe ve cinsel dokunulmazlığa karşı suçlar, fiziksel zarar verme, aşağılayıcı muamele ve kötü çalışma koşulları dayatılması yoluyla işçi haklarını ihlal etmekle suçlamıştı.
İspanya Ulusal Mahkemesi hâkimlerinden Antonio Piña, suç duyurusunu kısmen kabul etti. Buna göre hâkim, cinsel özgürlüğe karşı suçlar, fiziksel zarar verme ve aşağılayıcı muamele iddialarını soruşturacak. Ancak insan ticareti ve işçi haklarının ihlaline ilişkin suçlamaları soruşturma kapsamı dışında bıraktı.
Hâkim, ceza soruşturması başlatılması için yeterli delil bulunduğu kanaatine vardı. Kararında, tanık ifadelerinin yanı sıra savcılığın dosyaya sunduğu bir fotoğrafa da dikkat çekti.
Söz konusu fotoğrafın çalışanlardan birinin kolunda, "sert bir şekilde tutulmuş olabileceği ihtimaliyle örtüşen bir morluk" gösterdiğini belirten hâkim, aynı görüntüde kadının uyluklarından birinde başka bir kişinin ısırık izine karşılık gelebilecek iki işaretin de görüldüğünü kaydetti.
Şikâyette, söz konusu yaralanmaların kadın çalışanın cinsel nitelikli eylemlere zorlanmasının sonucu olduğu ileri sürülüyor.
83 yaşındaki Iglesias, Grammy ödüllü bir sanatçı olarak onlarca yıllık kariyerinde 300 milyondan fazla albüm sattı. Ünlü şarkıcı, hakkındaki suçlamaları "kesinlikle asılsız" olarak nitelendirerek hiçbir kadına "istismarda bulunmadığını, baskı uygulamadığını veya saygısızlık etmediğini" söyledi.

İspanya’da 83 yaşındaki şarkıcı Julio Iglesias hakkında gündeme gelen cinsel taciz ve saldırı suçlamalarına ilişkin yeni bir gelişme yaşandı. İspanya Ulusal Mahkemesi, Iglesias’ın Bahamalar ve Dominik Cumhuriyeti’ndeki evlerinde çalışan iki eski kadın personelin dava açılması yönündeki talebini kabul etti.
Ulusal Mahkeme Hakimi Antonio Pina’nın, kadınların cinsel saldırı, taciz ve aşağılayıcı muamele iddialarını içeren başvurusunu kabul ettiği bildirildi.
İspanyol basınında mahkeme kaynaklarına dayandırılan haberlere göre Hakim Antonio Pina, başvurunun kabul edilmesine ilişkin gerekçesinde şikâyetçinin ifadesinin ceza soruşturmasının başlatılması için yeterli ilk bakışta delil niteliği taşıdığını belirtti.
Pina’nın gerekçesinde, “Dava, davacının tek bir ifadesine dayanmaktadır ve bu ifade, ceza soruşturmasının başlatılmasını haklı çıkaracak nitelikte ilk bakışta delil teşkil etmektedir” ifadelerini kullandığı aktarıldı.
Dosyada yer alan iddialar, Iglesias’ın Bahamalar ve Dominik Cumhuriyeti’ndeki konutlarında çalışan iki kadının şikâyetlerine dayanıyor.
Kadınlar, basına yaptıkları açıklamalarda ünlü şarkıcıyı cinsel saldırı ve tacizin yanı sıra kendilerine tokat atmakla da suçladı. Şikâyetçiler ayrıca Iglesias’ın hem kendilerine hem de diğer çalışanlara yönelik sistematik biçimde aşağılayıcı davranışlarda bulunduğunu ileri sürdü.
İspanyol basınında yer alan haberlere göre iki kadının, 3 Şubat’ta İspanya Ulusal Mahkemesine şahsen başvurarak dava açılması yönündeki taleplerini doğrulamaları gerekiyor.
Julio Iglesias hakkındaki iddialara ilişkin hukuki süreç devam ederken, suçlamalar henüz kesinleşmiş bir yargı kararıyla hükme bağlanmış değil.

YENİ Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel sürecin takibi için TBMM’de kurulacak izleme komisyonuna üye vermeyeceklerini açıkladı: “Bundan sonra kimse bizi düşünerek hesap yapmasın. Tek başına demokrasicilik oynayanlar, buyursunlar oynasınlar.”
Özel, komisyon için partileri ziyaret eden TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş’la görüşmesinin ardından konuştu.
YENİ Parti lideri, ‘Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonu’ nda yer aldıklarını ve raporu sahiplendiklerini, ancak rapordaki ‘demokratikleşme’ konusuyla ilgili adım atılmadığını ve çok sayıda kişinin tutuklandığını belirterek şunları söyledi:
“Bugün bize geliyorlar, ‘Kanunun 6’ncı maddesinin 5’inci fıkrası gereğince silah bırakma için Meclis sorumluluk alsın, komisyon kursun, sen de gel, burada dur’ diyorlar.
Biz bugüne kadar hep analar ağlamasın diye doğru yerde durduk, şehit cenazesi gelmesin, ülke demokratikleşsin diye doğru yerde durduk ama artık şunu herkes bilsin ki, dün sabah Sözcü gazetesine, geçen hafta Halk TV’ye, ondan önce Tele1’e, T24’e kayyum atayıp hepimizin sesini keseceksin, sonra geleceksin ‘ Gelin birlikte bir şey yapalım, tarihe birlikte geçelim.’ “
Şahsi hesaplarla yürütülen böyle bir sürecin bundan sonraki aşamaları için kimse kendi şahsi hesabına bizi katıp, hesap yapmasın. Herkes şapkasını önüne koysun.
Elçiye zeval olmaz. Meclis Başkanı üzerine düşen görevi yapıyor. Kendisine de söyledim, yola çıktığımız gün taahhütler böyle değildi. ‘Ben bir taahhüdümü aksattım mı?’ dedim. Diyor ki ‘Siz yaşadığınız zorluklara rağmen bambaşka yapıcı yerde durdunuz.’ Neden? Bu ülke için? Taahhüdünü tutan var mı? Ondan sonra gelmişler, demokrasicilik oynayalım.
Bundan sonra kimse bizi düşünerek hesap yapmasın. Herkes şapkasını önüne koysun, hesabını, kitabını bizim varlığımıza ve yokluğumuza göre yapsın. Hesabını, kitabını bundan sonra bizim takınacağımız tutuma göre yapsın.
Biz bu işin içinde yokuz. Bizim bu işlerin içinde olmamızı isteyenler önce bu ülkeye tarih önünde verdikleri sözleri tutacaklar. Rapor orada, komisyon orada, bundan sonra tek başına demokrasicilik oynayanlar, buyursun oynasınlar.
Bir de makbul muhalefet partisi buldunuz, majestelerinin muhalefeti, tepe tepe kullanın. Seçilmiş, seçim kazanmış, sokakta peşinden on binler yürüyen, milyonları meydanları dolduran bir muhalefet sizin bulunduğunuz zemine meşruiyet kazandırmayacak. Majestelerinin muhalefetiyle istediğiniz yolu yürüyün.”
PKK lideri Abdullah Öcalan, 27 Şubat 2025’te ‘Barış ve Demokratik Toplum’ adını verdiği bir metinle PKK’ya silah bırakma çağrısı yaptı. Örgüt, 11 Temmuz 2025’te silah bıraktığını duyurdu, 30 örgüt üyesi Irak’ın Süleymaniye kentinde silahlarını bir varilde yaktı .
Süreç için Meclis’te kurulan ‘Milli Dayanışma Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonu’ nun AKP, MHP ve DEM Partili üç üyesi, 24 Kasım 2025’te İmralı Cezaevi’nde Öcalan’la görüştü . Görüşmenin tutanakları, 23 Ocak 2026’da TBMM’nin sitesinden yayınlandı .
Komisyon, 18 Şubat’ta da sürece ilişkin ortak raporu kabul etti. Bunun ardından İmralı heyeti Öcalan’la birçok kez görüştü.
Meclis, 10 Ağustos’ta PKK’nın silah bırakması için 12 maddelik ‘Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun’ u kabul etti. Kanun, 18 Ağustos’ta Resmi Gazete’de yayınlandı.
Yasa kapsamında yine süreç dört alt kuruldan oluşan Takip ve Değerlendirme Kurulu kuruldu.
O kurul, ilk kez 24 Ağustos’ta toplandı. Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz’ın başkanlık ettiği toplantıda şu isimler yer aldı: Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan, İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, Milli Savunma Bakanı Yaşar Güler, MİT Başkanı İbrahim Kalın, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genel Sekreteri Hakkı Susmaz ve MGK Genel Sekreteri Okay Memiş.
DEM Parti İmralı heyeti üyesi Pervin Buldan toplantıdan önce alt kurullar kurulacağını, Öcalan’ın da ‘silahsızlanma ve siyasallaşma kurulu’ nda görev alacağını söyledi . Fakat aynı isimde bir kurul açıklanmadı. Alt kurullardan ‘Silahsızlanma ve Stratejik Koordinasyon Alt Komisyonu’nun ismi Buldan’ın işaret ettiğine benziyor.
27 Ağustos’ta da DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti’nden Şanlıurfa Milletvekili Mithat Sancar, Öcalan’ın süreç için kurulan kurulda yer almasını beklediklerini belirtip “Önümüzdeki günlerde netleşmesini bekliyoruz” diye ekledi.
Bahçeli, 10 Ekim’de ‘siyasallaşma koordinatörlüğü görevinin Öcalan’ın hakkı olduğunu’ söyledi.

Kılıçdaroğlu ile görüşmesinin ardından aynı gün Yeni Yol Grubu ile görüşen Kurtulmuş, ziyaretin ardından basın mensupların açıklamalarda bulunup terörsüz Türkiye sürecinde TBMM'de yaklaşık bir yıldır devam eden çalışmalarda olumlu bir noktaya geldiklerini belirtmişti.
"Fikirler olgunlaşacak, önümüzdeki hafta da görüşmeleri tamamlayacağız." diye konuşan Kurtulmuş, "En kısa süre içinde TBMM 'de oluşturulacak izleme komisyonu, millet adına bu süreci takip ve kontrol etmek için çalışmalarına başlayacaktır." demişti.
Kurtulmuş, 11 Kasım'da ise AK Parti Grup Başkanı Abdullah Güler ile görüştü.
Görüşmenin ardından gazetecilere açıklamalarda bulunan AK Parti Grup Başkanı Güler, Kurtulmuş'un komisyona yönelik AK Parti TBMM Grubu'nun görüşünü aldığını aktarıp şöyle konuşmuştu:
“Kanunun adı, Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun. İzleme komisyonun adı da Kanunla beraber yer alacaktır. TBMM nezdinde, Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair İzleme Komisyonudur. Biz fikirlerimizi beyan ettik. Diğer parti grupları da beyan edecektir, ondan sonra ortaya bir tablo ortaya çıkacaktır.”
12 Kasım'da Bahçeli ile görüşen Kurtulmuş'un ziyareti ise yine 40 dakika sürdü.
Son olarak dün ise TBMM Başkanı, İYİ Parti Genel Başkanı Müsavat Dervişoğlu ile görüştü.
Görüşmelerde Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun kapsamında TBMM'de kurulacak İzleme Komisyonu hakkında fikir alışverişinde bulunulduğu öğrenildi.

İstanbul Eyüpsultan'da otomobilinde kırmızı ışıkta beklediği sırada silahlı saldırıya uğrayan iş hanı sahibi Ferhat Yamen (40), kaldırıldığı hastanede yaşamını yitirdi. Cinayetin şüphelisi olarak Alibeyköyspor Kulübü Başkanı Halil F. belirlenirken, saldırının yaklaşık 80 milyon lira değerindeki bir dükkanın satışından kaynaklanan anlaşmazlık nedeniyle gerçekleştirildiği iddia edildi. Firari şüphelinin yakalanması için polis ekiplerinin çalışmaları devam ediyor.
Olay, dün saat 15.30 sıralarında Eyüpsultan ilçesi Alibeyköy Mahallesi Atatürk Caddesi'nde meydana geldi. Bir iş hanının sahibi olan Ferhat Yamen, otomobiliyle iş merkezinin önündeki trafik ışıklarında beklediği sırada silahlı saldırıya uğradı.
Aracın yanına yaklaşan saldırgan, Yamen'e peş peşe ateş açtı. Vücudunun çeşitli bölgelerine kurşun isabet eden Yamen ağır yaralandı. İhbar üzerine olay yerine gelen sağlık ekipleri, yaralıyı ambulansla hastaneye kaldırdı. Ancak Yamen, doktorların tüm müdahalelerine rağmen kurtarılamadı. Olay yerinde yapılan incelemelerde 19 adet boş kovan bulundu. Saldırganın olayın ardından yaya olarak kaçtığı belirlendi.
Cinayetin aydınlatılması için Asayiş Şube Müdürlüğü ekipleri tarafından geniş çaplı soruşturma başlatıldı. Çevredeki güvenlik kameralarını inceleyen polis ekipleri, saldırıyı gerçekleştiren kişinin Alibeyköyspor Kulübü Başkanı Halil F. olduğunu tespit etti.
Soruşturma kapsamında elde edilen bilgilere göre, Ferhat Yamen ile Halil F. arasında yaklaşık 80 milyon lira değerindeki bir dükkanın satışından kaynaklanan anlaşmazlık bulunduğu öne sürüldü. Olayın ardından kaçan Halil F.'nin yakalanması için polis ekiplerinin çalışmaları sürüyor.
Hayatını kaybeden Ferhat Yamen'in cenazesi, otopsi işlemleri için Adli Tıp Kurumu morguna kaldırıldı. İşlemlerin tamamlanmasının ardından Yamen'in cenazesi bugün ailesi tarafından teslim alındı.
Ferhat Yamen'in cenazesinin yarın öğle namazının ardından Alibeyköy Veysel Karani Camii'nde kılınacak cenaze namazı sonrası Hasdal Mezarlığı'nda toprağa verileceği öğrenildi.

Rusya merkezli Azimuth Airlines'a ait Sukhoi Superjet 100 tipi yolcu uçağına, Mineralnye Vody-Antalya seferi sırasında bomba ihbarı yapıldı.
65 yolcu ve 4 mürettebatın bulunduğu bildirilen uçak için yapılan ihbarın ardından Antalya Havalimanı'nda güvenlik önlemleri artırıldı.
Havalimanının 2'nci pistine iniş yapan uçak, güvenlik prosedürleri kapsamında 5 numaralı apronda oluşturulan güvenli park alanına çekildi; yolcu ve mürettebat tahliye edildi.
Tahliyenin ardından güvenlik ekipleri ve patlayıcı madde uzmanları uçakta arama çalışması başlattı.
Antalya Valiliği, uçakta gerçekleştirilen aramanın ardından bomba ihbarına ilişkin açıklama yaptı.
Valilik açıklamasında, Antalya Havalimanı'na iniş yapan uçağa uzman ekipler tarafından hızlı şekilde müdahale edildiği ve uçaktaki 65 yolcu ile 4 mürettebatın güvenli şekilde tahliye edildiği belirtildi.
Açıklamada, patlayıcı madde uzmanlarının uçakta yaptığı aramada herhangi bir olumsuzluğa rastlanmadığı ve bomba ihbarının asılsız olduğunun tespit edildiği bildirildi.

TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş, Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel ile görüştü.
Yeni Parti TBMM Grubu'nda yaklaşık 40 dakika süren görüşme, basına kapalı gerçekleşti.
Görüşmenin ardından gazetecilere açıklamalarda bulunan Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özel, TBMM Başkanı Kurtulmuş'un, Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun kapsamında TBMM'de kurulacak "izleme komisyonu"na ilişkin siyasi partileri ziyaret ettiğini hatırlattı.
Kurtulmuş'a yapıcı tutumu için teşekkür ettiklerini belirten Özel, "Terörsüz Türkiye" hedefi kapsamında Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonunun kurulduğunu, daha sonra komisyon raporunun hazırlandığını anımsattı.
Terörün bitmesi, kanın ve gözyaşının durması için bütünleşik çözüm önerdiklerini aktaran Özel, süreçle sorunların demokratikleşme zemininde çözüleceğini dile getirdi.
Özel, Türkiye'nin ve dünyanın CHP'nin yönetim kadrosuna girdiği tüm seçimleri kaybetmiş bir kadronun getirilmesini ibretle izlediğini söyledi.
Demokratikleşmeye yönelik kararlılıklarını dile getiren Özel, Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonunda yer aldıklarını ve raporu sahiplendiklerini belirtti.
Özgür Özel, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: "Bugün Sayın Kurtulmuş, raporun 6. kısmının 5. maddesinde muallak olarak 'Meclis tarafından takip edilir' dendiği için bir takip komisyonu kurulması üzerine geliyor ve meselenin silah bırakma süreciyle ilgili kısmına indirgenmiş bir takip komisyonu öneriyor. 6. kısım kısım da, 7. kısım kısım değil mi? Ben Sayın Kurtulmuş'a, 'Bu süreçlerin peş peşe değil, iç içe sürdürülmesi gerektiğini' söylemiştim. Sayın Kurtulmuş da sorumluluk alacağını ifade etmişti. Sizler de tanıksınız. DEM Parti'nin Eş Genel Başkanlarıyla görüştüğümüzde de yaz boyunca demokratikleşme adımlarının atılacağını, 1 Ekim'den itibaren 7. maddeyle ilgili yasal faaliyetlerin sürdürüleceğini ifade etmişlerdi.
Bugün geldiğimiz noktada kasım ayının sonuna doğru yaklaşıyoruz. 6. maddeyle ilgili ilerlemede, silah bırakmayla ilgili bir taraf 'silahlar bırakılıyor' diyor, bir taraf 'bırakma değil, taşıma var' diyor, MİT Başkanı'nın ifadesidir. Bu kapıyı çalıp, 7. kısımdan bahseden yok. 7. kısmın en özelliği, Sayın Bahçeli'nin 'Ahmet'ler göreve' dediği kayyum uygulamalarının sona ermesiydi. Bunun için kanuna falan gerek yok. Hükümet, gerekli yetkisini kullanacak görevine iade edecek."
Bazı televizyonlara ve basın kuruluşlarına kayyum atandığını hatırlatan Özel, muhalefetin sessizleştirildiğini savundu.
Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonu raporunda Anayasa Mahkemesi kararlarının uygulanmasına yönelik hükümler yer aldığını aktaran Özgür Özel, Anayasa Mahkemesi ile Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi kararlarına uyulmadığını öne sürdü.
Özel, rapordaki "demokratikleşme" konusuyla ilgili adım atılmadığını, çok sayıda kişinin tutuklandığını aktararak, şunları söyledi: "Bugün bize geliyorlar, 'Kanunun 6. maddesinin 5. fıkrası gereğince silah bırakma için Meclis sorumluluk alsın, komisyon kursun, sen de gel, burada dur' diyorlar. Biz bugüne kadar hep analar ağlamasın diye doğru yerde durduk, şehit cenazesi gelmesin, ülke demokratikleşsin diye doğru yerde durduk ama artık şunu herkes bilsin ki, dün sabah Sözcü gazetesine, geçen hafta Halk TV'ye, ondan önce Tele1'e, T24'e kayyum atayıp hepimizin sesini keseceksin, sonra geleceksin 'Gelin birlikte bir şey yapalım, tarihe birlikte geçelim.'"
Ülke yararına olan her yerde olacaklarını dile getiren Özel, ülkenin yararına olan şeyin ise iktidar değişikliği olduğunu savundu.
"Şahsi hesaplarla yürütülen böyle bir sürecin bundan sonraki aşamaları için kimse kendi şahsi hesabına bizi katıp, hesap yapmasın. Herkes şapkasını önüne koysun" diyen Özel, seçim tarihine yönelik açıklamaları "Milletvekillerinin özgür iradesine ipotek koyma" olarak nitelendirdi.
Muhalefetin susturulduğunu savunan Özel, "Elçiye zeval olmaz. Meclis Başkanı üzerine düşen görevi yapıyor. Kendisine de söyledim, yola çıktığımız gün taahhütler böyle değildi. Ondan sonra gelmişler, demokrasicilik oynayalım." ifadelerini kullandı.
Özel, "Bundan sonra kimse bizi düşünerek hesap yapmasın. Herkes şapkasını önüne koysun, hesabını, kitabını bizim varlığımıza ve yokluğumuza göre yapsın. Hesabını, kitabını bundan sonra bizim takınacağımız tutuma göre yapsın." dedi.

Majestelerinin muhalefetiyle istediğiniz yolu yürüyün."

Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, 5 Kasım 2026'da fon soruşturması kapsamında tutuklanmıştı.
Fon soruşturması kapsamında Marmara Cezaevi'nde tutuklu bulunan bulunan Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya , saat 13.00 sıralarında rahatsızlandı.
Baygınlık geçirdiği öğrenilen Kaya, bunun üzerine Marmara Ceza İnfaz Kurumu Devlet Hastanesi'ne kaldırıldı. Tedavisinin ardından koğuşuna geri gönderildi.
Eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, 26 Eylül 2026'da AK Parti Genel Başkan Yardımcılığı görevinden affını istemişti.
Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya'nın, fon soruşturmalarından önce bir şirketin hisselerine 163 milyon TL yatırım yaptıkları, borsadaki likidite krizi ve fon çöküşünden hemen önce (Nisan - Eylül 2026 arası) bu hisseleri satarak 2,17 milyar TL haksız kazanç sağladıkları iddia edildi.
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı soruşturma kapsamında Kaya çiftinin mal varlıklarına tedbir talep etti; çift ise adliyeye giderek ifade verdi ve "özel bir bilgi veya yönlendirme almadıklarını" belirterek suçlamaları reddetti. Kaya çifti, ifadelerinin ardından SPK'nın getirdiği "gönüllü geri ödeme/etkin pişmanlık" mekanizmasından yararlanarak, borsadan kazandıkları yaklaşık 1,86 milyar TL'lik kâr kısmını TMSF'nin belirlediği hesaba iade etti.
5 Kasım 2026'da Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, suç örgütüne üye olmak ve SPK Kanunu'na muhalefet suçlamalarıyla tutuklandı.

At the IPO price, Anthropic is reportedly valued at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market round , but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago.
Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.
The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO.
Although none of Anthropic’s venture capital investors holds more than a 5% stake in the company, the IPO is a massive windfall for its numerous backers . Investors that own approximately 1% of the company reportedly include Sequoia and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC also holds about a 1% stake in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter. Other backers set to make billions are Iconiq, Menlo Ventures, Coatue, and Sound Ventures, a firm launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, and Spark Ventures, the only VC firm known to hold a board seat at the company.
Some of the company’s existing investors, namely Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter Capital Management, are so enthusiastic about Anthropic’s future that they were reportedly planning to buy billions of dollars’ worth of the company’s shares in the IPO.
Yet the investors’ holdings in Anthropic pale in comparison to those of the Claude maker’s strategic partners , Amazon, which owns nearly 15% of the company, and Google, which holds almost 14%. A group of major tech companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners, have also agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO.
The company’s seven co-founders , including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, according to the S-1 filing, bringing in about $282 million for each.

Anthropic has raised $81.3bn in the biggest initial public offering of all-time, leapfrogging SpaceX’s $75bn market debut in June.
The AI giant said in a statement late on Wednesday that the company and its seven co-founders had sold 980 million shares at $83 each.
The offering represents a significant scaling up of its IPO after Anthropic said last week that it intended to offer 825 million shares and between $70 and $78 apiece.
Anthropic shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.”
The blockbuster offering gives Anthropic a market value of roughly $1.5 trillion, making it the world’s 12th-biggest firm at current market valuations, just behind Tesla.
Anthropic’s market debut has been closely watched as a test of the eye-watering valuations of tech companies leading the rollout of AI.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c674:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has quickly become one of the most notable names in the technology industry.
Anthropic is poised to hit a value of more than $1.4 trillion (£1.1 trillion) when it debuts on the public stock market.
The artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the popular chatbot Claude said it will price shares at $83 each when it lists on Thursday on the Nasdaq, a tech-focused stock exchange based in New York.
That price will make it one of the most highly valued companies in the world.
It will be the first US firm focused exclusively on AI to go public, marking a crucial test for the fast-growing industry, which faces questions over whether the huge investment poured into the technology will be profitable.
The AI firm said earlier this month it would likely offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which valued the company at up to $1.3tn.
But demand for Anthropic's stock debut - commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO - is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke with the BBC on condition of anonymity.
The person said shares were more than 10 times oversubscribed ahead of the public listing, meaning demand for Anthropic shares exceeded the number of shares available.
If that turns out to be the case, Anthropic's valuation could quickly blow past its target on Thursday when trading begins.
Depending on how strong that demand is, Anthropic could even exceed the early market valuation of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which was the world's most highly valued stock debut when it went public with a value of $2.2tn in June.
However, in the weeks that followed, SpaceX shares fell significantly in price .
As it stands, Anthropic's listing will see the firm raise more than $68bn from its initial investors. It is also expecting another $26bn from private placements. So the total amount the company will raise is expected to be $94bn.
The amount of cash Anthropic has raised from its listing is already more than SpaceX raised in June .
OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and Anthropic's biggest AI rival, is expected to go public next year.
Until then, Anthropic will be the only public company in the US that is entirely focused on the technology, or one that was founded and built around AI tools and products. Its scope is different from tech giants like Google and Microsoft that also develop AI but are involved in other tech services.
The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
There is excitement around Anthropic's listing, but also some concern from investors around its ability to generate revenue and profits going forward.
Yang Wang, a principle financial analyst with Counterpoint Research, said the central issue for Anthropic is whether its business "can keep pace" as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years.
"Nevertheless, it is not an everyday occurrence for public investors to gain direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity," Wang said.
While nearly every other major tech company is pouring huge amounts of money into the technology and infrastructure required for their own AI tools, they are built around social media or online retail or online search. AI tools and applications are secondary.
"Anthropic going public gives us a whole new window into what AI demand looks like," Marta Norton, who heads investment strategy at investment firm Empower, told the BBC.
Anthropic was started by a group of co-founders , led by siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, all of whom left their work at OpenAI to start a new AI firm.
The company has carved itself out in the ongoing AI race as more focused on building the technology with safety top of mind.
It refused to comply with a demand by the US Department of Defense that Anthropic's tools be used in an essentially unrestricted way. And Dario Amodei has been outspoken in his belief that AI tools may soon be so powerful that they present a threat to human existence.
Nonetheless, the company is looking to grow quickly and gain more access to financing through the public markets in order to do so.
Norton said Anthropic going public now, in a time of market volatility comes down to the simple fact that the company needs access to more money.
"AI is financially demanding," Norton said. "The public markets open up the financial spigot a little bit more, and so the time has come."
But broader anxieties have started to grow about the AI industry's business model, which is reliant on expensive computer chips that are in short supply. The technology is also dependent on controversial data centres and funding such operations require deals with other tech companies.
The Federal Reserve Bank has expressed concern about the rapid growth of AI-related debt being financed through "complex and opaque" structures, according to minutes from its October meeting to discuss a potential rate rise.
A few of the meeting's participants also noted that "AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms".

Artificial intelligence firm positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, with trading slated to begin Thursday
Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83 on Wednesday, positioning the artificial intelligence company for one of the biggest initial public offerings in history. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange.
The pricing is above Anthropic’s earlier estimates. Last week, the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set its preliminary share price at $70 to $78. With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) from $1.26tn to $1.41tn. Elon Musk’s SpaceX debuted on Wall Street in June with the biggest market offering ever at $1.77tn. With Anthropic setting its share price at $83, it could now surpass SpaceX.
Amodei is planning to sell about $260m worth of shares with the IPO, as are his six fellow co-founders. At the top of the price range, the co-founders’ stakes will be worth more than $18bn each.
When Anthropic filed for its IPO last month, the company detailed rapidly rising revenue in its prospectus: $41m in 2023, $386m in 2024, $4.585bn in 2025 (an increase of more than 1,000%), then $16.286bn in the first six months of 2026 alone. The company disclosed that, as of the end of June, it had raised $141.1bn.
Despite the increasing revenue, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of $80bn for the first half of 2026.
Anthropic’s main expenditure listed in its investor prospectus is computing power from datacenters. The company has compute purchase commitments and lease agreements of more than $70bn over the next 12 months and more than $450bn by 2030, with a further $450bn due by 2045.
Anthropic is the first company at the forefront of the generative AI boom to go public, and its performance is likely to affect investors’ enthusiasm. Its competitor OpenAI was slated to hit Wall Street later this year, but CEO Sam Altman has said that the company opted to delay its IPO until it can overcome safety concerns.
Anthropic’s IPO comes during a volatile time for AI and the stock market. Last month, the industry saw a broader slowdown, with share prices dropping at several companies amid growing concern about the technology. Then, last week, Nvidia, which designs the chips AI companies use to power their chatbots, was racked with a scandal that led to CEO Jensen Huang resigning after reports of multiple extramarital affairs.

US loses measles-free status after 26 years in historic setback
The US has officially lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, as its largest outbreak in over three decades continues. The Pan-American Health Organization has declared measles endemic in the US, Bolivia and Mexico.
texts.https://www.wired.com/story/us-lost-meas:
The US has hit terrible twin milestones over the past week: Two more people died from measles , bringing this year’s death count to double digits, and the country officially lost its status as a country that had eliminated the highly infectious disease .
The US eliminated measles in 2000 and maintained that status for 26 years. Now, the nation faces an uphill battle to vanquish the virus once more, and it will take years to be measles-free again.
Noel Brewer, a professor of health behavior at the University of North Carolina, presented a report last week to the Pan American Health Organization showing continuous measles transmission for at least 12 months in the US—erasing one of the nation’s greatest public health achievements.
WIRED asked him how he felt after PAHO officials reached a consensus that the country was no longer measles-free. He paused.
“I have not actually thought about my reaction,” he says. After a beat, he says that the loss is “a somber moment for public health” that’s particularly wrenching because it’s a “completely avoidable situation.” Mexico and Canada have managed to wind down their outbreaks, but “measles in America is a runaway train,” Brewer says. “There's no end in sight, and it may even be gaining speed.”
PAHO director Jarbas Barbosa da Silva Jr. officially announced the change in status on Tuesday. “Losing a measles elimination status has broader implications than losing a public health designation,” he said at a press conference. “It means the virus has circulated for a prolonged period of time, putting families and communities at risk of preventable illness, hospitalization, and death.” Bolivia and Mexico also lost their elimination status this year; Canada lost it a year ago.
Brewer presented three key lines of evidence showing that measles has become endemic in the US. The outbreak in Utah and Arizona has gone on for more than 12 months, and the US has had measles cases every week since January 20, 2025. The genomic data also shows a great deal of similarity across states, indicating the clusters are closely linked—and each week, there are cases where the sources can’t be confirmed, indicating they didn’t come from travel or known contact with other patients.
“We have a problem on our hands,” says William Moss, epidemiology professor at Johns Hopkins. And it’s not going away anytime soon. To reclaim its status as measles-free, the US will have to prove it has gone a full year without continued transmission. That’s unlikely to happen under the Trump administration—and its actions have made it more difficult for future leaders.
“Reestablishing elimination is not just about reporting fewer cases—it also requires convincing the world that we have a strong enough surveillance system to find cases and deaths,” Jennifer Nuzzo, an epidemiologist and director of the Pandemic Center at Brown University, tells WIRED in a text.
The fact that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and state health departments differ on how many people have died from measles “is a sign of dysfunction,” Nuzzo says. There have been 10 confirmed measles deaths so far this year—seven in Pennsylvania, two in Wisconsin, and one in New York—but the CDC only lists six.
Such chaos also breeds distrust, says Frederic Bertley, president and CEO of the Center of Science and Industry. That's “a huge problem” for a public trying to parse who is telling the truth and whether they should listen, he says.
Even as measles was eliminated, anti-vaccine rhetoric began to rise , especially around the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine. Vaccination rates began falling—spurred in part by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an environmental lawyer turned anti-vaccine activist who published a now-retracted article alleging a link between vaccines and autism in 2005. He continued crusading against vaccines as head of Children’s Health Defense and at the helm of the Department of Health and Human Services during President Donald Trump’s second term.
The Trump administration has done little to stop the outbreaks, cutting billions in funding from state, local, territorial, and tribal public health departments and offering conflicting messages on vaccines. During a televised February 2025 cabinet meeting following the first child death in a decade, Kennedy said “it's not unusual, we have measles outbreaks every year.” The CDC hasn’t held a single press conference on measles throughout the entire outbreak; as PAHO was making its measles status announcement on Tuesday, HHS sent out an email about Kennedy’s cooking show.
“The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does,” CDC director Erica Schwartz said in a statement . “Losing a designation doesn't mean we abandon an evidence-based approach. It means we remain focused on stopping outbreaks.” Kennedy posted on X , “I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.”
To regain its elimination status, the US needs to address barriers to health care access, missed vaccination opportunities, misinformation, and vaccine hesitancy, Barbosa said. That includes mounting wide-reaching vaccination campaigns, expanding laboratory testing capacity, and responding quickly to cases, including contact tracing. It’s the bread and butter of public health, but the longer it takes to create a comprehensive response, the more it will cost, experts warn.
Future efforts to contain measles will require “a stronger centralized federal response to these outbreaks” paired with support for “very local responses,” says Moss. That means identifying communities with long-standing under-vaccination and understanding why, he says, as well as improving trust in public health guidance.
“Immunity gaps” tend to concentrate in specific geographic areas and communities, and national or even state-level data can “mask these significant inequalities, providing an incomplete picture of the population's actual level of protection,” Barbosa said.
The CDC announced $100 million in August and September—more than a year after the outbreak began—to help fund state and regional efforts to combat measles, but Congress will need to allocate $100 million to $400 million more for measles elimination in coming months, Brewer says.
“More than 90 percent of children get the measles vaccine, Brewer points out. “This is a vaccine that has extraordinary public support, and it goes across the aisle.”
But to achieve herd immunity, vaccination rates need to be at least 95 percent due to how contagious the disease is. High transmissibility also means measles is very hard to uproot once it begins to spread.
Yet ending national measles transmission is “its own reward,” Brewer says. It spares children’s lives, keeps them out of hospitals, and prevents blindness and other lifelong complications. “We no longer have that benefit,” he says. “Children are now being stalked by this incurable and deadly disease.”

Pennsylvania records eighth measles death of 2026, a day after the US formally loses its 26-year elimination status.
An unvaccinated resident of Pennsylvania has died after contracting measles, marking the eighth measles-related fatality in the northeastern state this year.
The Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) confirmed the death on Wednesday and said it had been reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
While the department did not publicly identify the individual who died, it said they were a resident of Clinton County, in the centre of the state.
The latest death comes shortly after the United States formally lost its measles elimination status, a designation it held for nearly 26 years.
That status indicated that measles was not endemic to the US, meaning no single strain had circulated continuously for 12 months or more.
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) , a branch of the World Health Organization, updated the US’s designation on Tuesday after reviewing transmission data from the country.
The US is grappling with its worst measles outbreak in more than three decades. As of November 12, the CDC had counted 5,412 confirmed cases since the start of the year.
Pennsylvania, meanwhile, reported 1,589 cases across 46 of its 67 counties. The state’s health agency pledged to continue its aggressive response to the outbreak.
“Approximately 300 DOH staff are proactively working with residents, community organizations, and health care providers to combat the measles outbreak in the Commonwealth through access to fact-based information and access to the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine,” the department wrote in a news release.
The agency also said state health officials have administered more than 11,500 MMR vaccine doses in 2026, including more than 7,200 shots in pop-up clinics since the outbreak erupted in late April.
Experts say vaccine hesitancy in recent decades has contributed to the rising number of cases.
Measles is highly contagious and can spread quickly, particularly when someone coughs or sneezes. The virus can survive for up to two hours in the air, and an estimated 90 percent of those who are not immune will catch it upon exposure, according to medical authorities.
Critics point to leadership under US President Donald Trump as contributing to the measles outbreaks.
One of Trump’s cabinet officials, Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, has questioned the efficacy and safety of vaccines like the MMR shot.
He also said in an interview with NewsNation that the MMR vaccine “contains a lot of aborted foetus debris and DNA particles”, an unsubstantiated claim.
Still, he encouraged vaccination in a social media post on Tuesday, following PAHO’s decision to revoke the US’s measles elimination status.
“We will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status. I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles,” he wrote.
The CDC also said it remained committed to stopping measles outbreaks and regaining the country’s elimination status.
“The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does,” CDC Director Erica Schwartz said.
Before taking office in early 2025, Kennedy claimed that no vaccine was “safe and effective” and promoted the discredited theory that vaccines cause autism.

Trump is stacking the FCC with Republicans, even as the Democrats boycott.
Senate commerce committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX) began a meeting Wednesday meant to confirm President Donald Trump’s nominee to the Federal Communications Commission with a lopsided dais. To his right sat all 14 Republican members of the panel, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD). To his left were about a dozen empty chairs — every Democratic member of the panel was absent.
Cruz said he’d learned the night before that Democrats intended to boycott the vote, though Democrats say they’d repeatedly raised their concerns about advancing a Republican FCC nominee without a Democratic one. “The administration has shown it’s willing to move Democrats,” Cruz said, pointing to Senate votes scheduled on bipartisan pairs of nominations to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission. And even though the Supreme Court confirmed his power to do so, Cruz said, Trump has not moved to fire any Democrats from the FCC , as he did at the Federal Trade Commission . “This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party,” Cruz said.
“This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party”
But in statements and comments to reporters outside the committee room, Democrats said that the process has been far from normal. Senate committees often vote on nominations to historically independent agencies in bipartisan pairs. Confirming Danielle Thumann Severs, senior counsel to FCC Chair Brendan Carr, to become a commissioner at the agency would put the FCC at four total members — three Republicans and one Democrat, Anna Gomez. Gomez’s term has technically expired, though she can remain on the commission through next year unless she’s replaced. But Democrats fear that by confirming a third Republican to the FCC, Trump might finally fire Gomez , because he’d no longer need her present for a quorum to vote on key actions.
Democrats asked for Thumann’s confirmation vote to be withheld until her nomination could be paired with a Democratic nomination. One way to do that would be to renominate Gomez. But so far, the president has not offered any Democratic nominees for the commission. Democrats said they made their concerns clear to Cruz, and added, “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In addition to the procedural concerns, Democrats worry about Thumann’s work as an adviser to Carr, and whether she was truthful about the matters she worked on. In a letter asking Cruz to delay her confirmation vote, Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM) detailed his concerns. At the November 10th hearing where Thumann answered committee members’ questions, she testified that she had “not worked with the Chairman on any media-related issues,” Luján noted in the letter. But documents obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request show that Thumann was “looped in” on various media matters, and “helped draft Skydance’s commitments that facilitated the 2 FCC’s approval of the Skydance-Paramount merger,” Luján wrote. “She also played a role in processing informal complaints related to CBS 60 Minutes alleged news distortion and she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” The FCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.
Even Cruz admitted concerns with Carr’s handling of Kimmel’s comments in the aftermath of conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s killing. But at Wednesday’s meeting, he said he “emphatically agree[s]” that Thumann had resolved any lingering worries about that. He added that his JAWBONE Act , which the committee previously passed, could directly address First Amendment violations by government agencies of either party. The bill would let individuals sue government officials if they illegally try to compel social media or broadcast companies to remove their speech. Sen. Jerry Moran (R-KS), who’d similarly expressed concern over the Kimmel incident, said he found Thumann’s responses on the subject “comforting,” including in a phone call earlier that morning where he said he’d expressed his “serious interest in how the FCC protects and promotes free speech, including free speech on broadcast.” On the call, he said, “she was able to satisfy me once again in her answers, including an explanation for her role at the FCC and her lack of engagement on this type of issue as the FCC made decisions.”
“If she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?”
Speaking to reporters outside of the hearing room ahead of the meeting, Luján accused Thumann of lying to the committee. “The questions that I have is if she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?” he said. Luján said he wants both Thumann and Carr to appear before the committee by the end of the year to answer lawmakers’ questions. Asked if he’d support using the committee’s subpoena power or even pursuing impeachment against Carr when Democrats regain power next year, Luján said his vote to confirm Carr as a commissioner under President Joe Biden is among his biggest regrets, and that while he hopes Carr will testify voluntarily, “everything should be on the table here to be able to get answers for the American people.”
When it came time to vote on whether to advance Thumann’s nomination for a final step of a vote on the Senate floor, all 15 Republicans voted “aye.” That gave Thumann enough votes for her nomination to advance to the Senate floor, where it’s expected to pass along party lines once scheduled. Still, the clerk listed off the names of the 13 Democratic committee members whose seats remained empty. There was no response.

Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, marking a historic milestone nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch.
NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, the most distant human-made object, has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after it was launched.
The spacecraft hit the milestone on Wednesday and is now about 26 billion km away, according to NASA.
A light-day is the distance light can travel in 24 hours, which means messages sent from Earth take a day to reach Voyager 1, and another day for teams on the ground to receive a reply.
The feat is “the best illustration of just how vast space is”, said NASA scientist Tiffany Kataria. “So much of what we dream about is travelling to other stellar systems,” she told the AFP news agency. “And it took Voyager 1 nearly 50 years to get to just the edge of our own solar system, let alone to only a light-day.”
Many exoplanetary systems, she noted, are at least several light-years away. NASA expects Voyager 1 to take about 18,000 years to travel a full light-year.
Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft to have reached interstellar space, the region beyond the Sun’s heliosphere. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035.
Some of Voyager 1’s equipment, including its cameras, has been switched off remotely to save power, but the probe continues to study invisible phenomena such as magnetic fields.
The data helps researchers study “the gas, the dust and other material that exists between stars”, Kataria said.
Both craft carry “Golden Records”, 30cm gold-plated copper discs intended to convey the story of our world to extraterrestrials.
Earlier in their journeys, the Voyagers explored the giant planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
Images of Jupiter taken by Voyager 1 first revealed the existence of rings around the planet and helped scientists understand the “really extreme vortices and weather” in its atmosphere, Kataria added.

One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.
Voyager 1 , launched in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, achieved a historic milestone on Wednesday: It became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft is so far away , that by the time its light reaches Earth, it comes from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on , and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.
“It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”
For Fran Bagenal, a planetary scientist at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who began working with Voyager 1 as a graduate student during its earliest years, the occasion is a momentous technological feat. “What's exciting is the fact that we have a spacecraft that was built in the mid ’70s that is still working,” she says. “Storing data on an eight-track tape that’s working on a spacecraft after 50 years—I mean, it’s amazing.”
Even as Voyager 1 approaches its 50-year anniversary next September, and its end of mission perhaps not long after that, the spacecraft is still checking items off its laundry list of scientific achievements. The spacecraft—alongside its twin, Voyager 2—was originally intended to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment to observe the outer planets .
But Voyager 1 kept traveling beyond the solar system and is now exploring the interstellar medium that fills the space between star systems. Voyager 1’s remoteness gives researchers a rare opportunity to study how the effects of the sun ripple even into the interstellar medium—and at what point those effects wane, says Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist for the Voyager Mission at Princeton University.
Just as both Voyager spacecraft are moving through space, so is our own solar system—only about 35,000 miles per hour slower, Badaruddin says. That means that as the pair continue their journeys, they’re sending back information about the space that our own sun and planet will pass through in about three years’ time.
“We can learn from telescopes and Earth-orbiting observatories, but there's really nothing like having a spacecraft in that environment that's sending us data,” Badaruddin says.
Voyager 1’s unprecedented journey isn’t without challenges. The craft has stayed in communication with Earth far longer than planned and is trekking through regions of space that it was never built to encounter or study. Researchers are helping maintain crucial functions, but they’re now doing so with a full day of lag in communications both to and from the spacecraft, Badaruddin says.
“Light time is really affecting us,” he says. “You factor it in. It’s like having a long commute.” Building new commands for the spacecraft is now a week-long process, for instance, since it takes time to receive data from the spacecraft, analyze it, and create a new command, he adds.
Still, the Voyager team is used to navigating unforeseen circumstances. For decades, they’ve been managing to make do with a dwindling power supply coming from the craft’s nuclear generators. In September, mission operations switched off some of Voyager 1’s devices in lieu of lower-power alternatives, a maneuver the team dubbed the “Big Bang.” The swap, which saved the craft 10 watts of power, kept mission operations from having to switch off another instrument as early as next summer.
Even when contact with Voyager 1 is eventually lost, the spacecraft will leave a lasting legacy—especially for any future such far-traveling missions, should NASA or another space agency launch one. A successor to Voyager might, for instance, have new devices such as a dust instrument to better analyze the interstellar medium or cameras to give astronomers a better view of these distant stretches of the cosmos, Rankin says.
“I would hope that the Voyagers and their reaching interstellar space has taught us the lesson that we've got to just keep reaching for the stars,” she adds.
Every mission must meet its end, though. And Badaruddin’s best guess is that Voyager 1’s could come in the next three to five years, as the plutonium-238 powering it decays further. Once the craft transmits its final signal to Earth, it will still continue its silent tour of the galaxy.
But Badaruddin acknowledges he’s part of a lineage of mission managers who have said that the spacecraft only has a few years left, only to be proven wrong . “The Big Bang was a rabbit we pulled out of a hat. As long as we can keep finding rabbits, we can keep going,” he says. “Don’t bet against Voyager.”

ABD Ulusal İstihbarat Direktörü (DNI) Jay Clayton , teknoloji şirketlerinin hizmetlerinde son günlerde art arda yaşanan kesintilerin "koordineli" veya "devlet destekli" saldırılardan kaynaklanmadığını belirtti.
Clayton, ABD Temsilciler Meclisi'nde düzenlenen "Dünya Genelinde Tehditler" oturumunda, hizmet kesintileri ve siber saldırı olasılığına ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu.
Çok sayıda ABD'li teknoloji şirketinin hizmetlerinde yaşanan kesintilere değinen Clayton, "Bugün elimizdeki bilgilere ve yaptığımız kapsamlı incelemelere dayanarak, bunların bakım ve teknik değişikliklerle ilgili ayrı hizmet kesintileri olduğunu söyleyebiliriz. Bunlar, koordineli veya devlet destekli saldırılar değildir" ifadesini kullandı.
Kesintilerin zamanlamasının soru işaretleri doğurduğunu ve bu durumu anladıklarını belirten Clayton, Amerikan halkının yaşananlar hakkında bilgi sahibi olmaya hakkı olduğunu vurguladı.
Clayton, "İstihbarat topluluğumuz, ABD ağlarını ve kolluk kuvvetlerimizi tehdit eden her türlü kötü niyetli siber faaliyet olasılığını izlemeye ve bu konuda tetikte olmaya devam ediyor" diyerek siber tehditlere karşı dikkatli olmayı sürdürdüklerini belirtti.
Dünya genelindeki tehditlerin değerlendirildiği oturuma Federal Soruşturma Bürosu (FBI) Direktörü Kash Patel katılmadı. Komite Başkanı Andrew Garbarino, Patel'in oturumda bulunmamasını eleştirdi.
Clayton, ABD ile İran arasındaki gerilimle bağlantılı İran kaynaklı tehditlerin güncelliğini koruduğunu ve istihbarat topluluğunun bu tehditleri yakından izlediğini belirtti. Clayton, özellikle Orta Doğu'daki gelişmeleri anlık olarak takip ettiklerini vurguladı.
Clayton, "ABD dışında ve içinde İran’ın ölümcül komplolarını tespit etmeye, caydırmaya ve bunlarla mücadele etmeye kararlıyız. Bu tehditler, son dönemde önemli ölçüde artmıştır" değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
ABD'nin yurt dışında görev yapan personelinin "daha büyük bir risk altında" olduğunu savunan Clayton, İran kaynaklı tehditleri anlamak ve bertaraf etmek için tüm istihbarat kapasitelerini kullandıklarını söyledi.
FBI Direktör Yardımcısı Christopher Raia, "Bu tehditlerle mücadeleye yardımcı olmak için İran tehdit görev merkezimizi yeniledik ve bu süreçte birçok başarı elde ettik" dedi.
FBI Direktörü Kash Patel'in oturuma katılmaması, çok sayıda Kongre üyesinin tepkisini çekti.

Democrats try to prevent quorum, say Thumann lied about not working on media issues.
A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote.
All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee’s 13 Democrats were absent. “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” Cruz said at today’s hearing.
Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January.
Although the Senate Commerce Committee generally requires one minority member to be present for nomination votes, a spokesperson for Cruz said Senate rules allow the nomination to be advanced for a vote in the entire chamber. A spokesperson for Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the committee, said in response that “since 2005, Commerce Committee rules required that a quorum include one member of the minority for official action on bill, resolution, or nomination.”
Technically, the committee has operated with no rules during Cruz’s chairmanship because Cruz “failed to pass committee rules” for the current session of Congress, Cantwell’s spokesperson said. “Nevertheless, in practice it has operated in line with rules from the last Congress (and this provision, specifically, since 2005), including that a quorum with a member of the minority party must be present for official action on a nomination or legislation. Until today.”
At a hearing last week, Thumann said she never worked with Carr on media-related topics, leading to accusations that she provided false testimony. “I have not worked with the chairman on any media-related issues,” Thumann said after Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) asked, “Do you support Chairman Carr’s illegal campaign to remove Jimmy Kimmel from the nation’s airwaves?”
“It appears that Ms. Thumann misled the Committee and offered false testimony, seriously calling into question her judgment and character and impeding the Committee’s work in determining whether she should be seated on the Commission,” Luján wrote in a letter to Cruz yesterday. “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related issues,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media-related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount.”
The FCC website describes Thumann as senior counsel to Carr on matters before the Wireline Bureau, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau, and the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau. Emails obtained in a public records request by the group Protect Democracy show she had some involvement in media-related matters.
Thumann provided follow-up responses to senators’ questions this week. She said that her work sometimes includes “reviewing documents or filings in a matter outside of my designated portfolio. However, I did not have any conversations with Paramount, CBS, or Skydance related to the merger.”
Thumann has been referred to as Thumann Severs in the nomination process, but she uses the name Thumann.
Luján wrote that Thumann “played a role in processing informal complaints related to” alleged news distortion on CBS’s 60 Minutes , and that “she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” However, Thumann was only a recipient of the Kimmel-related emails we found in a search of the messages.
The emails do show that Thumann approved language used in a response the FCC gave to complaints about the alleged news distortion in a 60 Minutes interview with Kamala Harris. The response informed people who submitted complaints that they should instead submit comments on an FCC docket that had been set up for the 60 Minutes proceeding.
“Hi Kristi, I have confirmed with the Chairman and Erin that we would like for complainants to be encouraged to resubmit their news distortion complaints in the relevant ECFS [Electronic Comment Filing System] proceeding,” Thumann wrote. “Can you please work on some draft language to send to consumers that would advise them on this step (including how to use ECFS)?”
Democrats announced yesterday that they would try to prevent a quorum for today’s vote. They objected to adding a third Republican to the committee while a Democratic seat remains empty.
“All Democratic members of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee object to the majority stacking independent commissions with Republicans and rushing nominees through the Committee process in this lame duck session with no Democratic pairs,” Cantwell said in a statement.
Cantwell and other Democrats on the committee sent a letter to Cruz urging him to cancel the vote, while quoting his own words from 2014. “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the Democratic committee members said.
Cruz said today that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January. But today is November 18.” Cruz said there is “ample precedent” for advancing nominations in a lame-duck session.
Senate Commerce Committee rules state that a quorum for nomination votes requires a “majority of the members, which includes at least one minority member.” But a Cruz spokesperson pointed to certain clauses regarding committee quorums in Senate rules when contacted by Ars today.
In the Standing Rules of the Senate , paragraph 7 of rule XXVI says that “no measure or matter or recommendation shall be reported from any committee unless a majority of the committee were physically present,” and does not have any requirement for minority members to be present. Elsewhere, the Senate rules say that when a committee reports a measure to the Senate floor, “no point of order shall lie with respect to that measure” as long as the committee took its action “in conformity with the requirements of paragraph 7 of rule XXVI.”
While committees can have different quorum rules, a Cruz spokesperson said this functions as a “cleansing clause” so that “earlier procedural irregularities, such as a violation of a committee rule, cannot be used to invalidate the vote on the Senate floor.”
FCC nominations have traditionally been paired with one Republican and one Democrat when there is an empty seat for each party. But Cruz said that’s not a requirement.
“There’s nothing that requires the president to nominate in pairs… the law merely says that no more than three of the commissioners may be from the same party,” Cruz said during the Republican-only meeting.
The Communications Act prohibits a single party from holding more FCC seats than is necessary to form a majority. It says, “The maximum number of commissioners who may be members of the same political party shall be a number equal to the least number of commissioners which constitutes a majority of the full membership of the Commission.”
Republicans would have a 3-1 majority on the FCC if Thumann is confirmed by the Senate. The sole Democrat, Anna Gomez, would have to leave at the end of 2027 if Trump does not nominate her for another term.
“There is no mandate for the outgoing majority to rush through a partisan FCC nomination in its final weeks… Ms. Thumann Severs’ nomination should be postponed until the next Congress and paired with Commissioner Gomez’s renomination and the nomination of an additional Democratic commissioner,” Democrats told Cruz in their letter this week.

MyMems, from the creator of SimCity and The Sims, is a new social simulator powered by AI.
Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims , is working on a new game — and it’s built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems . Like Wright’s other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. “We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world,” he tells The Verge .
The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a “social simulation” with worlds “built from your memories and the people who shaped you.” You can add “memories” to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are generated into pieces you can place on the game’s map. Your worlds can also include AI-powered avatars, which can represent people you know in your life. Ideally, as you play, the planet starts to become a “map of your psyche,” kind of like Inside Out , Wright says. Worlds can be private, but you can also share them with others.
Here’s another way to think of it, from Virginia McArthur, executive producer and GM at MyMems developer Gallium Studios: “It’s a cozy world builder with a really deep social simulation underneath.”
I’ll admit that I don’t totally get it, and it seems like a tricky idea to grasp without playing it. Still, as heady of a concept as it might be — turning your memories into a game world — Wright and team still want it to be fun. “This isn’t meant to be your legacy diary necessarily,” says Anthony Maitz, a product manager at Gallium Studios. “It’s meant to just be something you kind of play around with.” However, Maitz notes that what you’re working toward is a “proxy” of you — a word that seems to be the inspiration of the game’s earlier title, Proxi: Yesterday’s You Tomorrow . The game will use the “Behavior Engine” from a company called Artificial Agency , which makes AI tech for video games, as a “foundational technology.”
Like other industries, gaming is starting to reckon with generative AI. Early AI virtual worlds created with models from a startup backed by a Pixar cofounder and Google’s Project Genie weren’t experiences you’d actually want to spend dedicated time with, and indie developers I spoke to in March were largely opposed to the technology . But AI technology has taken some big leaps this year with companies like Google , Meta , and Roblox now letting users make games with AI right from their phone, and retro gaming becoming overrun with AI-powered ports of classic titles.
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said earlier this year that generative AI has “zero part in what Rockstar Games is building” with GTA VI . But even as a recent industry survey indicated that more game developers are starting to use generative AI as part of their job , workers are pushing back against generative AI use , and the technology is at the center of fierce debates over indie game awards .
Many players are rejecting AI outright, and I wondered if the Gallium Studios team was worried about opposition toward MyMems ’ use of AI. Wright says he has three boys at home and that they are all “pretty negative” on AI. He attributes negativity over AI to be toward the meaning of art and authorship and credit, a concern he calls “well-founded.” But he also calls AI an “amazing tool.”
“We’re not making slop,” says McArthur. But Maitz notes that while the team has “been concerned” about a negative response to the generative AI use, they’ve learned that people don’t mind when they use AI in a “ Scribblenauts -y style” for things like having the game make a high school. The team also found that people got “addicted” to a test app with a character creator, including Maitz’s own daughter, who he says “hates” AI. “By making it so that the player is authoring it over and over, bit by bit, it doesn’t really feel like you cheated,” Maitz says.
MyMems , which is set to launch in 2027, will join a growing field of other social simulations, like Krafton’s Inzoi and Nintendo’s smash hit Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream . But none quite have the pull of The Sims , which remains one of EA’s most important franchises. With The Sims , Wright says that many people tried making their real families in the game.
“It was interesting how people really were naturally trying to map this game, which was like a little toy, onto their real life,” he says. With MyMems , that’s what the team is trying to do the “follow-through” on — what if they made the whole game focused on you?
Imagine opening a family scrapbook and the way people and things jump out, Wright explains. “As you go through more and more pages, pretty soon you have this whole little circus of people and events and things from your life.” It’s chaos, he says. “I want something that feels kind of like that.”
Update, November 18th : Added context about Artificial Agency.

Bu sonuçla siyah-beyazlı takım, organizasyonda 6. galibiyetini aldı. Real Madrid ise 5. yenilgisini yaşadı.
Karşılaşmaya sert savunma yaparak başlayan Beşiktaş Fuzul, Gabriel ve Wilbekin'ın kazandırdığı sayılarla 7. dakikada 14 farklı üstünlük yakaladı: 16-2. Çabuk toparlanan Real Madrid, hücumda üretkenliğini kaybeden siyah-beyazlı takım karşısında üst üste bulduğu basketlerle farkı 3'e kadar indirdi. Beşiktaş, ilk periyodu 18-15 önde tamamladı.
İkinci çeyreğin başında dış atışlardan üst üste 3 isabet sağlayan siyah-beyazlılar, 12. dakikada farkı yeniden çift hanelere çıkardı: 27-17. Kalan bölümde de skor üretmeye devam eden ve bu periyotta 3 sayı çizgisinin gerisinden 7 basket kaydeden Beşiktaş Fuzul, soyunma odasına 45-37 üstün gitti.
Üçüncü periyodun ilk 6 dakikasında iki takım da skor üretmekte zorlandı. Karşılıklı basketlere sahne olan son 4 dakikada dış atışlardan kritik basketler bularak üstünlüğünü sürdüren siyah-beyazlı ekip, son bölüme 64-54 önde girdi.
Dördüncü ve son çeyrek büyük bir heyecana sahne oldu. Real Madrid, Smith'in dış atışıyla 37. dakikanın başlarında farkı 4'e düşürdü: 71-67. Eflatun-beyazlılara Jeffries'in kritik basketleriyle yanıt veren Beşiktaş, sahadan 83-79 galip ayrıldı.
Basketbol Avrupa Ligi'nin (EuroLeague) 12. haftasında ağırladığı İspanya ekibi Real Madrid'i 83-79 mağlup eden Beşiktaş Fuzul'de başantrenör Dusan Alimpijevic, tarihi bir galibiyet aldıklarını söyledi.

US secretary of state’s comments come as vulnerability in programming language Java highlighted
There is “zero evidence” that a wave of IT outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access, affected Apple and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or are the work of malign actors, according to the US secretary of state.
Marco Rubio said the US was “not under systemic attack” and a cascade of network problems was “not inter-related”.
In recent days, Microsoft , major US banks , Apple , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency have all been affected by technical failures and outages.
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber-hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.
Rubio’s comments came as cybersecurity researchers flagged a vulnerability in Java, a programming language used by 90% of companies in the Fortune 500, a ranking of the largest companies in the US. The researchers at US-based Calif used AI to discover the flaw and recently unearthed glitches in PHP, another computer language.
Calif said the Java flaw could allow hackers to remotely execute code, allowing them to place malicious software on a target’s systems.
The US director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, said the incidents were caused by security upgrades – such as plugging the flaws in PHP – that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.
“Everybody recognises it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” he told the Fox Business news channel.
Tal Be’ery, a cybersecurity expert, said he did not believe the incidents were linked directly but had a common underlying theme: AI. IT systems were buckling under the pressure of adding AI or tackling flaws uncovered by AI, he said.
“Our IT infrastructure is brittle, and when AI puts massive extra pressure on it, whether through upgrades to accommodate AI or through the rapid patching that AI-driven vulnerability discovery demands,” Be’ery said.
Since April, when the AI startup Anthropic released its Mythos model, which had a startling ability to flag IT flaws, the amount of vulnerabilities found by leading tech companies has soared eightfold – while OpenAI has also released models capable of finding previously unseen flaws. Researchers at Calif used OpenAI technology to discover the Java flaw.
“[Java] is the beating heart of the modern economy,” Calif wrote in a blogpost . “Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems.”
However, Steven Murdoch, a professor of security engineering at University College London, said the flaw did not apply to every Java user and was specific to a library of code – Base64 – that comes bundled with a version of Java.
“It’s significant but it’s not every Java program that is affected,” he said.
In the UK the National Cyber Security Centre urged organisations to keep their systems up to date, while the US and South Korean authorities also urged Java users to install security updates.
Rubio made the comments as he travelled with Donald Trump for key meetings in the Philippines on Wednesday, before flying to the tech hub of Shenzhen in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the outages on Tuesday. “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila.
The series of outages began on Thursday last week, when Microsoft’s email and other tools went down , affecting millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the problem to “an earlier network capacity upgrade”.
Flights across the US were grounded the next day in the longest “ground stop” since the September 11 attacks. The US Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.
By Monday, banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical problem at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related”.
The same day, United Airlines said it had resolved an internal system outage that delayed departing flights.
Then on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance”. Apple also confirmed problems with its iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday but said it had resolved them.
The Democrat Mark Warner, the vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, supported the assessment that the outages were not caused by a “coordinated effort” but by attempts to shore up systems.
“The evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”
Cynthia Kaiser, a former deputy director in the FBI’s cyber division, said it was “plausible” that the race to upgrade systems was fuelled by warnings that specific cyber adversaries were planning attacks.
Kaiser, now an executive at cybersecurity firm Halcyon, said she was more concerned about cyber criminals and scammers trying to “capitalise on the confusion to steal money from organisations and everyday people ”.
