Milli Savunma Bakanı Yaşar Güler, TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonunda, Milli Savunma Bakanlığının 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmelerinin ardından milletvekillerinin sorularını yanıtladı.
Bakan Güler, dünyada ve bölgede yaşanan krizlerin, artan çatışmalar ve değişen tehdit ortamının, ülkeleri savunma harcamalarını artırmaya, askeri kabiliyetlerini geliştirmeye ve modernizasyon faaliyetlerini hızlandırmaya yönelttiğini anlattı.
Küresel ölçekte savunma harcamaları artmaya devam ederken, Türkiye'nin de savunma harcamaları çalışmalarını kararlılıkla sürdürdüğünü belirten Güler, "Özellikle İran'ın hedef ayrımı gözetmeyen saldırılarının da ortaya koyduğu üzere, hava ve füze tehditleriyle insansız hava araçlarının yaygınlaşması güçlü, çok katmanlı ve bütünleşik hava savunma sistemlerine duyulan ihtiyacı daha da artırmıştır." diye konuştu.
Güler, bahse konu gelişmeler karşısında Çelik Kubbe, milli muharip uçak, dronlar ve insansız sistemler gibi öncelikli projelerin hızlandırılmasına, hava savunma kabiliyetlerinin güçlendirilmesine, kritik tesis ve altyapıların korunmasına, mevcut sistemlerin modernizasyonuna, yeni nesil tehditlere karşı çok yönlü tedbirlerin geliştirilmesine öncelik verdiklerini vurguladı.
Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın iradesi ve destekleriyle 2026, 2027 ve 2028 yılları için hususi olarak bütçe tahsis edilmesinin önemine işaret eden Güler, hususi bütçe tahsisinin savunma sanayisinin seri üretim kapasitesinin artırılması ve ihtiyaç duyulan sistemlerin hızlıca envantere kazandırılması bakımından büyük önem taşıdığını söyledi.
Güler, savunma bütçesindeki artışın temel gerekçesinin, değişen güvenlik ortamının ortaya çıkardığı ihtiyaçlar doğrultusunda savunma sanayisinin üretim kapasitesini ve Türk Silahlı Kuvvetlerinin caydırıcılığını güçlendirerek, Türkiye'nin güvenliğini uzun vadede teminat altına almak olduğunu belirtti.
Bakanlık olarak şehitlerin emanetlerine sahip çıkmayı, gazilerin ve ailelerinin yanında durmayı, ihtiyaç ve taleplerini duyarlılıkla yaklaşmayı öncelikli görev gördüklerini dile getiren Güler, şunları kaydetti:
"Bu anlayışla gazilerimizin ve vazife malullerimizin sosyal ve özlük haklarını daha da geliştirmek, hayatın her alanda karşılaştıkları sorunlara çözüm üretmek ve ailelerimizin refahını artırmak için devletimizin imkanları ölçüsünde Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığımızın koordinesinde çalışmalarımızı sürdürüyoruz. Nitekim ağustos ayında Gazi Meclisimiz tarafından kabul edilen ilgili kanunla bu konuda önemli adımlar atılmıştır. 7594 sayılı kanunla erbaş ve er şehitlerimizin anne ve babalarına aylık bağlanmasında uygulanmakta olan asgari ücret alt sınırının tüm şehitlerin anne ve babalarına uygulanmasına bakıma muhtaç gazilere ödenen bakım yardımının asgari ücretin 2 katından 2,5 katına çıkarılmasına erbaş, er, gazi ve vazife malulleri için maluliyet derecesinin yeniden değerlendirilmesi talep etme yaşının 41'den 55'e çıkarılması sağlanmıştır. 3713 sayılı kanun kapsamındaki erbaş ve erler ile korucu ve sivillere bağlanacak aylıkların alt sınır ve göstergeler oranında artırılması, terörle mücadelede malul kalmayacak şekilde yaralananlardan derece belirlenenlere bağlanan aylıkların artırılması ve terörle mücadelede terörist silahıyla malul kalmayacak şekilde yaralananlara aylık bağlanması ve bazı haklar verilmesi imkanı da getirilmiştir."
Bakan Güler, 2027 Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu teklifine göre, Şehit Yakını ve Gaziler Programı'nda tüm kamu idareleri için 30 milyar 25 milyon lira ödenek tahsisi de öngörüldüğünü ifade etti. Bahse konu ödeneğin koordinasyonundan Aile ve Sosyal Hizmetler Bakanlığının sorumlu olduğunu belirten Güler, yönetiminin ise Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığınca gerçekleştirileceğini söyledi.
Bakanlık bütçesine tahsis edilen ödeneklerin ise sadece ilama bağlı borçlar kapsamında yapılan ödemeler için olduğunu anlatan Güler, "Şehit yakınlarımıza ve gazilerimize yönelik hakların geliştirilmesinin yanı sıra, uzman erbaşlarımızın da özlük hakları ve kamu görevlerine geçiş imkanları dahil personelimizin geleceğine ilişkin iyileştirmeleri de yapıyoruz." dedi. Güler, bu kapsamda eğitim seviyesi uygun olanların 3. dereceden 1. dereceye yükselebilmelerinin sağlandığını belirtti.
"Bitirdikleri yüksek öğrenim süresine göre ilave kademeler ile 1 derece verilmesine imkan tanınmış uzman erbaşların astsubaylığa statü geçiş kontenjanları artırılmış, devlet memurları ile birlikte uzman erbaşların konutlardan faydalanma oranı yüzde 10'dan yüzde 20'ye çıkarılmıştır. Bunların yanı sıra emeklilik sürecine ilişkin olarak 55 yaşında yaş haddinden emeklilik hakkı getirilmiş, devlet memuru olarak istihdam edildikten sonra emekli olanların ise emekli aylıklarının doğrudan emekli olan uzman erbaşların emekli aylıklarıyla eşitlenmesi sağlanmıştır. Emeklileri dahil uzman erbaşlara 3600 ek göstergeden faydalanma hakkı verilmiştir."
Uzman çavuşların kamuya geçiş süreçlerinin mevcut mevzuat çerçevesinde yürütüldüğünü söyleyen Güler, sözleşmeli erbaş ve erler içinde de önemli iyileştirmeler yaptıklarını vurguladı. Bu kapsamda, görev şartlarının ağırlığı dikkate alınarak özel harekat ve operasyon tazminatından yararlanmalarının sağlandığını ve tutarın 63 bin lira seviyesine ulaştırıldığı aktaran Güler, "Sözleşme bitiminde ödenen tazminatlarda ise yüzde 33 oranında artış yapılmış böylece 7. hizmet yılını tamamlayarak ayrılan personele 2 milyon lira üzerinde ödeme gerçekleştirilmektedir. Bakanlığımız bünyesinde kalarak uzman erbaşlığa geçen sözleşmeli erbaş ve erlere de ikramiye imkanı getirilmiş. Uzman erbaşlığa geçiş için başvuru şartı 3 yıldan 2 yıla indirilmiştir." ifadelerini kullandı.
Bakan Güler, C-130 tipi askeri kargo uçağının kazasına ilişkin, "C-130 kazasına ilişkin analiz ve sonuçların değerlendirilmesine yönelik çalışmalarımız son aşamaya gelmiştir. Bu aşamada uçağın ana üreticisi Lockheed Martin tarafından incelenmesi talep edilen ilave parçalar gündeme gelmiştir. C-130 uçakları dünyanın birçok ülkesinde yaygın olarak kullanılmaya devam edilmektedir." bilgisini verdi.
Güler, firmanın incelemelerini tamamlamasının ardından kamuoyunu bilgilendireceklerini sözlerine ekledi.
Bakan Güler, Hürmüz Boğazı'nda enerji sevkiyatı aksadığında veya Kızıldeniz'de ticaret gemileri tehdit altında kaldığında, bunun sonuçlarını Türkiye'nin de hissettiğini söyledi.
Özellikle Orta Doğu ve çevresindeki krizlerin Türkiye'ye etkilerini yönetebilmek için Suudi Arabistan ve Pakistan'la mevcut savunma işbirliğine kalıcı ve kurumsal bir zemine oturtmak için anlaşmayı (Mekke Anlaşması) imzaladıklarını ifade eden Güler, anlaşmanın hiçbir ülkeyi hedef almayan savunma amaçlı bir işbirliği ittifakı olduğunu vurguladı.
Güler, anlaşma taraflar arasında savunma alanında düzenli istişare ve koordinasyonu geliştirmeyi, karşılıklı desteğe dayalı güvenlik ihtiyaçlarına cevap vermeyi amaçlayan bir çerçeve sunduğunu ifade etti.
"Öngörülen bu karşılıklı destek, muharip kuvvetlerin herhangi bir tehdit karşısında doğrudan veya ivedi biçimde konuşlandırılması anlamına kesinlikle gelmemektedir. Esas olan şu ki saldırıya uğrayan tarafın ihtiyaç duyduğu desteğin niteliğini belirleyerek talepte bulunması öngörülmektedir. Buna göre sağlanabilecek desteğin türü ve kapsamı, tehdidin ölçeği, niteliği, ilgili ülkenin ihtiyaçları ve tarafların milli değerlendirmeleri doğrultusunda ele alınacaktır. Ayrıca NATO üyeliğimizden doğan hak ve yükümlülüklerimiz de anlaşmanın 12. maddesiyle saklı tutulmaktadır."
Bu işbirliğinde temel ölçünün Türkiye'nin güvenlik ihtiyacı olduğuna işaret eden Güler, şöyle devam etti.
"Binlerce yıllık kadim devlet aklının önemli bir yansıması olan Türk Silahlı Kuvvetlerimiz, köklü tarihinden daima ilham ve ibret almaktadır. Bu anlayışla ortak çıkarımızın bulunduğu alanlarda hazırlığımızı önceden yapıyoruz. Bir kriz çıktığında ise olayın anlaşma kapsamına girip girmediğini ve Türkiye'nin hangi katkıyı sunacağını somut şartlara göre değerlendiriyoruz. Sonuç olarak Türkiye'nin hangi sorumluluğu hangi şartlarda üstleneceğine Türkiye kendi anayasal…

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies .
“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of want to give him space to figure this out,” Nadella said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
Huang stepped down last week from his CEO role, which he has held for 33 years. Huang’s leadership has been central to Nvidia’s ascent to one of the world’s most valuable companies, but his judgment was questioned after it was reported that he had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy feeding information back to Beijing. It was also revealed that Huang was having affairs with two Nvidia employees, including one who was a direct report.
While the world waits to see what the long-term economic impacts of Huang’s departure might be, Nadella says he still has confidence in Nvidia, which is a close partner of Microsoft.
“I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella added. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO at Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I’m in touch with the same set of people I was in touch with before [Huang left], so I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”
Microsoft is not unlike Nvidia in that its founder Bill Gates inhabited a larger-than-life persona as CEO.
“Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing, so that is pretty magical… They’re singular, but they’re not gods, right?” Nadella said. “I used to say to Bill [Gates]… Founders also die, and so at some point, a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over.”

With MyMems , Wright says he wants to “turn the simulation inward.”
The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.
MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.
“If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”
In an accompanying announcement video , Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”
Wright said MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your memories into self-contained areas that Wright compared to the various parts in a theme park: Sports, vacations, injuries, memories, and deaths could all be the basis for their own zones to play in. Players will also have the option to create worlds based on shared memories with family, friends, and co-workers, for example.
Since this is 2026, it shouldn’t be surprising that MyMems is making heavy use of generative AI (with a “proprietary behavior engine” on top) to transform your typed-up memories into simulated locales and characters. In the announcement video, Wright praises the “entirely open-ended” AI systems Gallium is using “to extract from the stories and whatnot based upon the memories you put into the game.”
But Wright’s focus on mining memories for simulation content predates the current generative AI boom. What has now become MyMems started off as Proxi , a mobile simulation that was first announced in 2018 as “a game of self-discovery, a game where we actually uncover the hidden you.” But after years of pre-production work (as outlined in an excellent Vulture piece earlier this year ), Wright’s Gallium Studios finally ran out of funding in late 2024, leading to mass layoffs for the small team and an uncertain future for the project.
Now the idea has been revived thanks in large part to a partnership with AI middleware firm Artificial Agency . Until now, that company has mainly been focused on agentic systems that can create “virtual players” to playtest a game or serve as a partner for human players.
Now, Artificial Agency’s marketing says the company’s AI tool will be used to create “a personal behavior model and a knowledge graph” from players’ memories, drawing some unsettling comparisons to big tech surveillance.
“Meta knows what you click,” the company writes. “Netflix knows what you watch. Nobody knows what you remember. MemDNA learns from your memories locally and only with your permission.”
Wright said the partnership with Artificial Agency will let Gallium benefit from “off-the-shelf” AI solutions without having to “become an AI research company” in its own right. He also said the collaboration will help limit costs by providing a cheaper option than the “really expensive” frontier models that might be overkill for a project like this.
“Right now AI has opened a vast new design area and I’m enjoying, you know, exploring that as a designer,” Wright said.

Söz konusu karar, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarındaki geleceğine ilişkin soru işaretlerini artırırken ABD ile Çin arasındaki yarı iletken rekabetini de yeniden gündeme taşıdı.
Nvidia'nın açıklaması, şirketin 17 Kasım'da gerçekleştirdiği mali sonuç toplantısında geldi. Kress, 25 Ekim'de sona eren çeyrekte Çin'e lisans kapsamında 2,4 milyar dolar değerinde Hopper serisi ürün satıldığını, ancak gelecek döneme ilişkin sevkiyat beklentilerinde Çin'e yönelik bu ürünlere yer verilmediğini söyledi.
Kress, şirketin artık Çin'e lisanslı Hopper veri merkezi ürünleri göndermediğini belirtirken kararın gerekçesine veya sevkiyatların ne zaman yeniden başlayabileceğine ilişkin ayrıntı paylaşmadı. Dolayısıyla Nvidia'nın bu adımının kalıcı bir satış yasağı mı yoksa mevcut koşullara bağlı bir sevkiyat durdurma kararı mı olduğu henüz bilinmiyor.
Nvidia'nın açıklaması, Çin'e yönelik bütün ürün satışlarının sona erdiği anlamına gelmiyor. Karar, özellikle Hopper ailesindeki veri merkezi ürünlerini kapsıyor. Bu ailenin en önemli işlemcilerinden biri olan H200, yapay zeka modellerinin eğitilmesi ve çalıştırılmasında kullanılıyor. Şirketin daha düşük kapasiteli ve ihracat kurallarına uygun bazı ürünleri içinse farklı bir tablo söz konusu.
Nvidia'nın son kararı, tek başına alınmış bir şirket kararından çok daha büyük bir mücadelenin parçası. ABD'nin Çin'in gelişmiş yarı iletkenlere erişimini sınırlandırması, Pekin'in yabancı teknolojiye bağımlılığı azaltma politikası ve iki ülkenin yapay zeka alanında üstünlük kurma çabası, bugünkü tablonun oluşmasında etkili oldu.
Üstelik Washington ve Pekin'in Nvidia çiplerine yönelik politikaları her zaman aynı yönde ilerlemedi. ABD bazı işlemcilerin ihracatına izin verirken Çin yönetimi aynı ürünlerin ülkeye girişini sınırlandırdı. Bu durum, Nvidia'yı iki farklı düzenleyici sistemin arasında bıraktı.
ABD, Çin'in gelişmiş yarı iletkenlere ve bu çipleri üretmek için kullanılan teknolojilere erişimini sınırlandırmak amacıyla Ekim 2022'de kapsamlı ihracat kontrolleri uygulamaya başladı. Washington yönetiminin temel gerekçesi, gelişmiş işlem gücünün Çin ordusu tarafından kullanılabilecek yapay zeka sistemlerinin geliştirilmesini kolaylaştırmasıydı.
Kısıtlamalar, Nvidia'nın A100 ve H100 gibi yüksek performanslı veri merkezi işlemcilerini de etkiledi. Şirket, Çin pazarındaki faaliyetlerini sürdürebilmek için ABD'nin belirlediği teknik eşiklere uygun, performansı sınırlandırılmış ürünler geliştirmek zorunda kaldı.
Washington, Ekim 2023'te kuralları güncelleyerek yalnızca işlem gücünü değil, çiplerin bellek bant genişliği ve işlem yoğunluğu gibi teknik özelliklerini de kapsayan yeni sınırlamalar getirdi. Böylece şirketlerin mevcut kuralları aşmak için daha düşük performanslı işlemciler tasarlaması da zorlaştı.
Nvidia'nın Çin pazarı için geliştirdiği H20 işlemcisi, ABD'nin ihracat kurallarına uyum sağlamak amacıyla performansı sınırlandırılmış ürünlerden biriydi. Ancak ABD yönetimi Nisan 2025'te bu işlemcinin Çin'e ihracatı için de lisans zorunluluğu getirdi.
Kararın ardından Nvidia, satılamayan H20 ürünleri ve üretim taahhütleri nedeniyle 2026 mali yılının ilk çeyreğinde 4,5 milyar dolarlık gider kaydetti. ABD yönetimi Ağustos 2025'te bazı Çinli müşterilere H20 gönderilmesine izin veren lisanslar verse de bu kez Çin yönetiminin kısıtlamaları devreye girdi. Nvidia'nın mali raporlarına göre şirket, Çin'in kendi sınırlandırmaları nedeniyle bu ürünlerin tamamını satamadı.
Bu gelişme, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarında karşılaştığı sorunun yalnızca ABD'nin ihracat politikalarıyla sınırlı olmadığını gösterdi. Şirket bir taraftan Washington'ın belirlediği teknik sınırları aşmadan ürün geliştirmeye çalışırken diğer taraftan Pekin'in yerli çip üreticilerini destekleyen politikalarıyla karşı karşıya kaldı.
ABD ile Çin arasındaki gerilime rağmen Donald Trump yönetimi, Aralık 2025'te Nvidia'nın H200 işlemcilerinin belirli Çinli müşterilere satılmasına izin verileceğini duyurdu. Bu karar, Nvidia'nın Çin pazarına yeniden erişebilmesi açısından önemli bir gelişmeydi.
ABD Ticaret Bakanlığına bağlı Sanayi ve Güvenlik Bürosu (BIS), 13 Ocak 2026'da ihracat lisanslarının değerlendirilmesine ilişkin politikasını değiştirdi. Daha önce reddedilme ihtimali esas alınarak değerlendirilen bazı gelişmiş işlemciler için artık belirli güvenlik koşullarının sağlanması durumunda başvuru bazında inceleme yapılabilecekti.
Bu düzenleme yalnızca Nvidia H200 işlemcisini değil, AMD'nin MI325X modeli gibi benzer özelliklere sahip ürünleri de kapsıyordu.
İzin, koşulsuz bir satış serbestisi anlamına gelmiyordu. ABD yönetiminin belirlediği şartlar arasında Çin'e gönderilecek ürünlerin ABD'deki müşterilere ayrılan küresel üretim kapasitesini azaltmaması, Çinli alıcıların ihracat kurallarına uyum ve müşteri denetimi için yeterli güvenlik prosedürlerine sahip olması, çiplerin sevkiyat öncesinde ABD'de bağımsız bir kuruluş tarafından teknik ve güvenlik testlerinden geçirilmesi ve ihracatın belirlenen performans ve güvenlik sınırları içinde kalması bulunuyordu.
H200 satışları için getirilen bir diğer dikkat çekici koşul ise yüzde 25'lik gümrük tarifesiydi. Çiplerin Çin'e gönderilmeden önce ABD'ye ithal edilmesi ve gerekli denetimlerden geçirilmesi öngörülüyordu. Bu süreç, satışın maliyetini ve lojistik koşullarını da değiştirdi.
Böylece ABD, Nvidia'nın Çin'e tamamen sırtını dönmesini istemeyen ticari yaklaşımı ile gelişmiş işlem gücünün Çin'in askerî ve stratejik kapasitesini artırabileceği yönündeki güvenlik kaygılarını aynı politikada buluşturmaya çalıştı. Ancak bu kez de Pekin'in onayı ve yerli üreticileri önceleyen politikası, planlanan satışların önünde engel oluşturdu.
ABD'nin H200 satışlarına izin vermesi, Çinli teknoloji şirketlerinin bu işlemcilere kolayca erişebileceği anlamına gelmedi. Çin yönetimi, Nvidia'nın gelişmiş işlemcilerine yönelik ithalatı sınırlandırarak yerli yarı iletken üreticilerini desteklemeye yönelik politikasını sürdürdü.

Elon Musk, who spent $277 million to get Donald Trump re-elected president in 2024 and who, during that campaign, declared himself “dark MAGA” and who, after the election, was subsequently photographed sporting a cartoonishly large MAGA hat while visiting the Oval Office, has some news for Americans: none of that necessarily makes him MAGA.
“I’m not MAGA,” Musk declared Wednesday, during a conversation with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the Dealbook Summit. Musk joined the conversation via video call, as he is currently in China, joining President Trump for the APEC summit.
“Well, at least I’m not like — I’m not sure what MAGA means,” he backtracked. “If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”
The comments were made amidst a broader question about how Musk felt in the wake of this year’s midterms, during which a “Blue Wave” led to Democratic victories throughout the country. Musk, notably, spent a gargantuan amount of money (reportedly some $445 million ) to support Republican candidates. Musk admitted Wednesday that such vast political spending might not have been a good use of his money.
“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seen much for it,” he said. “Or maybe it would have been much worse without that. But it certainly shows that, you know, American elections are not just about money.”
During his conversation with Sorkin, Musk also seemed to lean away from his viral edgelord persona and claimed that he held no extreme views. He said: “I don’t think I have like, you know, any any kind of extreme political views.”
Sorkin pushed Musk on this a little, noting that some people found his views on immigration extreme, to which Musk said: “Like what?” Mild laughter spread throughout the audience.
Ironically, the last time Musk spoke at Dealbook, in 2023, he was in the middle of a very public battle with his social media site X’s advertisers. Critics had accused Musk of platforming a typhoon of hateful content on his site, and advertisers were threatening to walk over it. In response, Musk famously told Sorkin that he hoped those advertisers would “go fuck” themselves .
Now, Musk has an entirely new set of concerns. Democratic lawmakers in various committees have signaled that they may investigate Musk and his business activities as they probe potential corruption throughout the Trump administration.
Specifically, officials have said they’re interested in scrutinizing Musk’s role in DOGE , the “government efficiency” initiative that Musk launched inside the White House at the start of Trump’s new term, as well as Starlink’s activities in Ukraine, where the company has been accused of throttling the military’s access to its internet service .
Sorkin broached some of the potential concerns for the Tesla CEO: “You hear people like the chairman of the oversight committee saying ‘lawyer up’ and you hear the president saying ‘if I have to give him a pardon’ — meaning you — ‘I’ll give him a pardon’.”
Musk replied: “I don’t think I need a pardon by the way, because I haven’t committed any crimes.”
Musk then made one of those controversial statements he’s known for, appearing to compare an incoming Texas official to Lavrentiy Beria, the top head of the Soviet secret police under Josef Stalin.
“The incoming Texas, you know, House Majority Leader, said that I should go to prison,” Musk said. “I’m like, the guy’s trying to you know channel Beria from, like, Stalin, where it’s, you know, show me the man, I’ll show you the crime type of thing.”
It’s not clear who (or what) Musk was talking about. Texas doesn’t have a House Majority leader. However, he may have been referencing Gene Wu , who is the incoming chair of the Texas House Democratic Caucus, and who has suggested that Musk be investigated for potential criminal activity.
“Hopefully, in this country, you still need to do an actual crime before you go to prison,” Musk added.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.
Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the Dealbook Summit.
“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”
He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”
He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”
But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”
When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast , Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”
He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

During his appearance at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella lamented the fact that a lot of America’s software systems — including those governing everyday hardware and transportation systems — suffer from unfixable software vulnerabilities that, in the age of AI-aided cyberattacks, are just waiting to be exploited.
“Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable,” Nadella said. “I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.”
In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches.
The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. Concerns have swirled that these outages are the result of cyberattacks, although officials have denied those claims. Still, the reality of AI-aided cyberattacks is spurring companies to find new strategies for vulnerability discovery and remediation.
Nadella touched briefly on the recent Outlook situation, noting that the global inconvenience was the result of a “latent bug” that led to a “perfect storm.”
“We put out an incident response, and we’re going to obviously take all of the learnings, both upstream architectural, as well as operational, and fix that,” he added.
“Somebody was telling me about sort of even the transportation systems and the amount of stuff that’s discoverable but with unpatchable firmware,” Nadella also added on the topic of vulnerable systems. “So we’ll have to really modernize for sure … and then we will have to assess what the threat vector looks like, what our own ability to both detect and then defend in real time looks like.”
Nadella made a broader point as well, which is that the process of patching software vulnerabilities has escalated to match the speed of potential exploitation, but that this has caused more problems.
“We now have a very powerful tool that finds vulnerabilities,” he said. However, companies used to have more time to test those patches, understand a situation, and deploy them, he said. At the same time, AI has made sophisticated cyberattacks much easier to enact.
“The patch [now] needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production, because it’s being exploited in the wild, right? So that’s going to create instability.”

Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change.
“Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.”
On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang.
“He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?”
Musk also signed a petition , alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back.
“[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…,” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”
He has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades,” Musk added. “He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him… and many of them are there because of him, and have higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”
Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey also said that he thinks Nvidia is making the wrong decision by not reinstating Huang.
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said earlier in the day at the DealBook event. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”
Musk also did not express concern over what Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could mean for U.S. national security.
“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.”
Other peers in the industry, like Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , reaffirmed their faith in Nvidia to move forward without its founder and CEO of 33 years at the helm.
“It’s the Nvidia board’s decision, but I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella said at DealBook. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took time during a high-level diplomatic summit in Asia on Wednesday to try and soothe public US jitters over a spate of cyber-related disruptions.
Rubio insisted authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors."
His comments, on the sidelines of a Southeast Asia summit, follow multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay, as well as the outage of a top-secret US government communications network.
"The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever, we have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other," Rubio told reporters in Manila while on a trip to Asia with US President Donald Trump.
"The second is that we have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind."
Rubio emphasised the ubiquity of technology when explaining why it could feel as if there was a growing wave of cyber incidents.
"The more technology becomes embedded into our everyday lives, the more the vulnerabilities become real," he said.
"There was a time when people used to physically go in with masks and guns and rob banks. Now they can do it from behind a computer screen halfway around the world and every major economy in the world is facing that same challenge."
On Tuesday a top-secret network that the National Security Agency (NSA) uses for internal communications went down, the agency acknowledged.
The NSA said it had experienced "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," but that its capabilities remained operational and "our ability to defend national security continues."
The NSA, part of the US Department of Defence, is responsible for global monitoring, collection and processing of information for intelligence and counterintelligence.
The Trump administration has insisted Americans and their various systems remain secure, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin emphasizing that the wave of recent outages does not stem from cyber criminals.
"I can tell you with complete certainty that we are not under attack," Mullin told CNBC. "There's no cyber threat that's taking place. The homeland is very secure."
Air travel was disrupted because of what the Trump administration called outdated equipment, causing regulators to halt all flights from taking off for several hours on Friday evening.
The mess of stranded travellers and aircrews spilled into the weekend and early this week.
Microsoft also suffered a major outage last week that affected Outlook and Teams users around the world, while several large banks saw disruptions to their banking apps and online portals on Monday.
Trump's rival Democratic Party, which just won decisively in US midterm elections earlier this month, blamed the administration's incompetence for the string of high-visibility outages and the lack of transparency around them.
"We've had the Microsoft incident, then we had the nationwide ground stop. Now we have concerns as it relates to highly classified servers over at the NSA," Hakeem Jeffries, a top Democrat in Congress, told reporters.
"I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves, so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America."

Measles became endemic in the US months ago—and it’s only accelerating.
International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “ shameful ” and a “ national embarrassment .” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.
The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.)
For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.)
According to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.
The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.
The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.
But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.
In a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.
Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.
Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas —that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.
“Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer said, and the national data shows multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.
For people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.
Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in big outbreaks in Arizona and Utah . But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”
To date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.
For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.
But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.
With the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action plan” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.
While the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.
A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data , only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Israeli tanks advance beyond the ‘Yellow Line’, forcing Palestinians to flee again as Gaza faces a deepening humanitarian crisis.
Israeli forces have launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the line they withdrew to under last year’s ceasefire and forcing Palestinian families, many of whom had already been displaced, to flee their homes once again.
The operation, the first major ground offensive publicly announced by the Israeli military since the ceasefire took effect on October 10, 2025, follows a warning by the United States-backed Board of Peace that the 13-month-old agreement risks collapse. In a report to the United Nations Security Council, the board accused Israel of restricting aid and delaying the deployment of Palestinian police, and Hamas of continuing armed activity and taxing goods entering Gaza. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”.
Israeli tanks and bulldozers advanced towards Salah al-Din Street, Gaza’s main north-south route, east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and north of the Bureij refugee camp, Al Jazeera correspondents reported. Palestinians fled those areas, amid heavy gunfire and artillery shelling.
The Israeli military body overseeing civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territory, known as COGAT, said the army had closed that stretch of Salah al-Din Street and told residents to stay away until further notice. The army hasn’t said how long the operation will last.
An Israeli attack on al-Mughraqa killed one person and wounded several others, an official at al-Awda Hospital told Al Jazeera. Separate attacks in Deir el-Balah, Nuseirat and Gaza City killed three more people.
“We fear this may be the start of a broader operation and that displacement will begin anew, as we have not yet recovered from the effects of the previous war and displacement,” Mahmoud al-Saafin, a 27-year-old resident of Bureij, told the AFP news agency.
The areas targeted in the operation lie west of the “Yellow Line”, where Israeli troops pulled back to under the first phase of President Donald Trump’s plan, leaving them in about 53 percent of Gaza. Israel has, however, continued to move that line gradually, and it now encompasses around two-thirds of the enclave. More than two million Palestinians live in the rest, mostly in tents.
The military told AFP it had launched “a precise operation” west of the line “to remove a threat” posed to the Israeli army, adding that “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area, adding it was responding to Hamas ceasefire violations.
“We reserve the freedom to act and manoeuvre whenever necessary to eliminate any immediate threat in the Gaza Strip,” the army said.
Israel says Hamas has been regrouping and rearming, and it has stepped up attacks. On Saturday, an Israeli attack killed Samir Abu Younis, the Qassam Brigades’ Rafah commander.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel won’t withdraw until Hamas is dismantled. “If tensions escalate on the various fronts, we are fully prepared to seize additional territory, evacuate local residents and incorporate it into Israel’s permanent security perimeter,” he said.
Hamas called the operation and the forced evacuations northeast of Nuseirat “a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement”, and urged mediators to “intervene immediately”.
It accused Israel of “systematically” squeezing Palestinians into a narrow area of Gaza, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s caretaker government of escalating to escape its domestic crises.
Hamas also condemned the Board of Peace for having “unacceptably equated the occupation’s ongoing aggression with the suffering of the Palestinian victim”.
The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine called the operation a “prelude” to a wider escalation aimed at forcibly displacing Palestinians.
Israeli forces have kept up near-daily attacks, shelling and home demolitions. Gaza’s Ministry of Health says they have killed 1,658 Palestinians and wounded 6,000 since the ceasefire began. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed in the same period, the Reuters news agency reports.
On Tuesday alone, Israeli fire killed six Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, Gaza’s civil defence agency and hospitals told AFP.
Aid remains restricted. About 100,000 tents are waiting to enter Gaza, held up by crossing closures and lengthy Israeli security checks, the International Organization for Migration says.
The ceasefire halted major fighting, but the rest of the plan, covering Israel’s withdrawal, reconstruction and Hamas’s disarmament, has stalled. Hamas agreed in July to a roadmap to give up its weapons and hand over governance. Israel rejected it.
Israel also hasn’t let the board’s technocratic administration start work in Gaza. That has held up an international stabilisation force, The Associated Press news agency reported.
The board spelled out what failure would mean. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”

A Gaza security source told AFP there was "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of Nuseirat refugee camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and air strikes since midday".

"There is Hamas infrastructure in the area in the central Gaza Strip," the military said, adding that the operation involved military and Shin Bet security agency personnel.
Residents of the affected areas told AFP they had fled for their safety, many of them not for the first time.
In addition, three Palestinians were killed and a number of people wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday, according to Gaza's civil defence agency.
One man was killed near the Nuseirat camp, one in Gaza City and one outside the Deir el-Balah police station in the central Gaza Strip, the agency said. It was not immediately clear whether the three attacks were linked to the ground operation.
The Israeli military told AFP that in the first two strikes it targeted "terrorists" and that it was not aware of the third attack.

Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas called the operation "a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement and confirmation that the occupation has reneged on its obligations".
The military told AFP that it was responding to Hamas ceasefire violations.
Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the US-brokered ceasefire deal that came after two years of war.
More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Football players say they are ‘traumatized’ after being handcuffed and detained by police while waiting for rides home
Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them , prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.
The plaintiffs sued Omnilert, the company behind the AI gun-detection system, Baltimore county police, the board of education, individual officers and the school principal, alleging unlawful detention and search because of technological and human errors.
“These students were failed not only by a technology that is prone to false alerts, but also by the very adults meant to keep them safe when we send them to school,” said Damon Hewitt , the president and executive director of the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, which is representing the students. “Instead of this protection, they were met with guns and traumatized. And it could have been even worse.”
The incident took place last fall. The students had just wrapped up football practice on the evening of 20 October when their coach passed out bags of Doritos to the team, according to the complaint. Taki Allen, a junior at the time, took several bags and was with his friends near the picnic tables waiting for their ride, when six local police cruisers emerged with lights flashing. Many officers unholstered their weapons and the students put their hands in the air, the complaint said.
The legal complaint stated that the plaintiffs “were in shock and feared for their lives after being stopped, ordered to their knees, handcuffed and searched” by armed officers. One officer allegedly told them as he left the scene: “Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem.”
The complaint described a chaotic series of events in which Omnilert’s AI gun-detection system flagged the chips bag as a firearm with 90% confidence. Omnilert Gun Detect system scans security footage for signs of firearms. “That alert kept going even after school staff and local police reviewed the image and determined it was a mistake,” the lawsuit stated.
While Omnilert markets its product as reliable and leading to “fewer false positives”, the lawsuit states that Maryland’s office of the inspector general for education “found that more than 99% of OGD Alerts in Baltimore County Public Schools were false positives that required no police response”.
Omnilert, the school principal, Baltimore police and the board of education did not immediately respond to a Guardian request for comment.
An Omnilert spokesperson previously told the Baltimore Banner that the company was reviewing the lawsuit and was “truly sorry for the fear they and their families experienced. We understand why they want answers.” A spokesperson for Baltimore county told the New York Times that the district cannot comment on pending litigation.
The lawsuit included texts from the school principal making light of the incident in messages to fellow administrators that contained emojis of a smiley face crying with laughter. The complaint said she did not apologize to the students.
One officer allegedly said as he began to leave the scene: “Fucking Omnialerts” and: “Stupid AI cameras.” His colleague allegedly joked to the plaintiffs: “Be careful on school property, especially holding stuff like that … be careful with your chips bags.”
The students didn’t find that funny, and reported feeling pain from tight handcuffs, as well as lasting emotional distress, according to the complaint.
Taki Allen said he no longer feels safe waiting for rides or hanging out at school after hours; he often pays for rides home to avoid waiting for rides from friends or family.
Freida Winfield, whose son Keith is part of the lawsuit, was en route to pick up him and his friends when they were detained. “ No child in Baltimore county should face this kind of danger while waiting outside his own school for a ride home from his mother,” said Winfield.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela on Wednesday, state TV reported, during an unexpected visit to Caracas.
Hegseth was received by Venezuela's interim leader, Delcy Rodríguez, in the capital ahead of a planned visit to Colombia later Wednesday.
"We see this as a renewal of our defence partnership and an opportunity for our two great armed forces to work together," Hegseth said, according to footage broadcast by VTV, Venezuela's state television channel.
The trip, which had not been publicly announced by the Pentagon, marks another step in the rapprochement between Washington and Caracas following the capture in January of Nicolás Maduro.
The cooperation agreement announced by Hegseth and Rodríguez provides for the resumption of technical and military cooperation between Washington and Caracas, which had been suspended for years amid deteriorating diplomatic relations between the two countries.
According to the Venezuelan leader, one of the main objectives is to strengthen the training of Venezuelan armed forces personnel through joint training and cooperation programmes. Rodríguez said the initiative would help improve the military's preparedness to respond to shared threats.
The agreement also aims to improve the operational equipment available to Venezuelan forces and provide access to new technologies. So far, neither government has provided details on the timeline for implementing the agreement, the resources to be allocated or the specific mechanisms through which cooperation will take place.
Rodríguez took power after Maduro was captured, although her continued leadership of the country remains shrouded in uncertainty. Her interim mandate expired in July and there is still no announced date for the next presidential election.
The rapprochement between Washington and Caracas has also been marked by agreements over Venezuelan oil and by the United States' strategy against drug trafficking in the Caribbean and the Pacific, which has caused the deaths of at least 240 people since September 2025 in attacks on vessels suspected of carrying drugs.
Hegseth's visit is part of efforts by Donald Trump's administration to expand its influence in Venezuela. The defence secretary is the third member of Trump's cabinet to travel to the country this year, following trips by the interior and energy secretaries, focused on Venezuela's oil and mineral resources.

Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago
Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro , to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
Speaking outside the recently reopened US embassy in Venezuela’s capital, Caracas, on Wednesday, Hegseth said: “It’s a great honor to be here as the first United States secretary of war this century to set foot in Venezuela.​ Just one year ago my presence here … would have been deemed impossible, almost unimaginable.
“In fact, exactly one year ago today … [Maduro] stood on a stage not too far from here and yelled mockingly, ‘Come and get me!’” Hegseth recalled, before adding sarcastically: “Well, we answered that call.
“The reality is that … January 3 is the day that will go down in history as a day of liberation for Venezuela,” Hegseth claimed, although Maduro’s allies continue to hold power with US support.
Earlier in the day, Hegseth was welcomed to the Miraflores Palace by Maduro’s former vice-president, Delcy Rodríguez , who became acting president with Donald Trump’s blessing after his abduction.
In the aftermath of the deadly US attack, Hegseth was one of the bluntest Trump administration voices when it came to celebrating the invasion. “Maduro had his chance … he effed around and he found out,” the defense secretary bragged .
Speaking at the palace, Hegseth struck a more conciliatory tone as he vowed to deepen cooperation with Venezuela’s new leaders in brief comments that were broadcast by the state broadcaster VTV.
“I stand here on behalf of President Trump, who sends his greeting and looks forward to the opportunities, not just militarily … but also economically: the incredible resource capabilities that your country has, that we look forward to unlocking together with you,” Hegseth told Rodríguez and senior cabinet members, including the defense and foreign ministers, Gustavo González López and Oliver Blanco.
Hegseth said his visit to Rodríguez’s “beautiful country” was designed to re-establish and increase “defense cooperation” between “two great militaries” that less than a year ago were briefly at war. Earlier this month, the New York Times reported that Trump officials were trying to negotiate a long-term US troop presence in Venezuela as part of their push for regional hegemony.
“I appreciate your leadership and commitment to your country,” Hegseth told Maduro’s successor, a once outspoken anti-imperialist leftist who has overseen an unlikely realignment with Washington since her ally was grabbed.
During her five-minute address, Rodríguez, whose oil-rich country is widely seen to have become a US protectorate after January’s invasion, made no mention of Maduro, who is behind bars in New York City.
But referring indirectly to his capture and the subsequent reconciliation with Washington, she told Hegseth: “Thanks to the political and geopolitical maturity of our governments, we have – in a very short period of time, just a few months – turned what were very difficult and very tough times for our people, into an extraordinary space for cooperation and mutual benefit.”
Rodríguez hailed the “historic” energy deal her government recently struck with Trump, who has called it “the biggest oil deal in world history” as well as “the spoils” of his “conquest” of Venezuela.
Hegseth claimed the agreement, which reportedly involves 65bn barrels of reserves, “makes the strait of Hormuz a non-factor for the western hemisphere”.
Critics of Rodríguez’s political movement painted Hegseth’s visit as a humiliating act of genuflection for a president with no choice but to roll out the red carpet for the man whose troops captured her boss.
Writing on X, Luz Mely Reyes, a prominent Venezuelan journalist, said Hegseth’s visit was designed to underscore Washington’s “direct administration” of her country.
“Ten months after Nicolás Maduro’s capture, Washington no longer needs to fire shots to remind everyone who is in charge: the mere presence on Venezuelan soil of the architect of the January incursion reaffirms that the country’s operational sovereignty is subject to the White House’s directives,” Reyes said.
Reyes suspected the visit also carried a message for members of Venezuela’s armed forces. “Domestically, the trip forces the military high command to legitimize the man who directed the extraction of their former commander in chief,” she said. “In this regard, I wonder whether it might be a message of discipline intended to prevent any pockets of resistance in the barracks.”
Trump’s attempts to expand his Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition of Latin American governments suffered a major blow last month with the defeat of his far-right ally, Flávio Bolsonaro, in Brazil’s presidential election. The leftwing winner, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has indicated his country will not join the initiative.
But Venezuela’s interim government is in little position to resist. During his surprise visit to Venezuela, Hegseth said Venezuela had gone from being “our most aggressive regional threat to [being] a compliant security partner”. He praised Rodríguez for working “closely, pragmatically, and diligently with the United States to stabilize Venezuela”. Hegseth claimed US and Venezuelan armed forces would work together to attack “narco-terrorists” operating on Venezuelan soil, vowing: “We will hunt you down. We will find you. And we will kill you.”
Concluding her speech at the palace, Rodríguez told her foe-turned-friend: “Thank you, secretary, and I wish you a lifetime of happiness.”

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing a resumption of military cooperation with Venezuela and vowing to crack down on drug traffickers. The trip marks the highest-level US visit since the ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January, signalling a dramatic shift in relations between the two countries.
Embattled US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced appearance in Caracas on Wednesday, the highest-level US visit since the January ouster of president Nicolas Maduro .
During the surprise stopoff en route to Colombia , Hegseth announced renewed US-Venezuelan military cooperation and vowed to "hunt" down drug traffickers.
"We will hunt you down, we will find you, and we will kill you," he said after announcing the deal that marks a dramatic thaw in long-hostile relations.
"You will no longer export your crime and your misery to America, to Venezuela , or any other country in the region," he added, referring to "narco-terrorists."
Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez hailed a "resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries" after years of rupture and US sanctions .
She has governed Venezuela with Washington's backing since US special forces captured Maduro and spirited him to New York , where he faces trial on charges of "narco-terrorism."
Read more Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro and wife Cilia Flores deny US torture charges as 'false accusations'
The American embrace of Maduro's former vice president has not gone down well among the country's often-repressed pro-democracy opposition.
While Venezuelans enjoy more freedoms than a year ago, US President Donald Trump 's administration has allowed swaths of the authoritarian state apparatus to remain in place.
Hundreds of political prisoners remain behind bars and no date has been set for free and fair elections .
But Venezuela is seen as vital for US efforts to secure new sources of oil, isolate Cuba 's communist government and curb cocaine trafficking from South America.
Caracas has long been accused of harboring Colombian drug-running guerrilla groups including the ELN, which operate across vast tracts of territory on either side of the border.
Hegseth, who recently avoided congressional impeachment and faces sustained scrutiny for his handling of the Iran war and the legality of deadly anti-drug strikes, later traveled to the Colombian capital Bogota.
Read more Rubio kicks off tour in Latin America as US vies for regional influence
Since Trump returned to office two years ago, the United States has significantly escalated military operations in Latin America.
US forces have struck alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, killing more than 230 people, according to an AFP tally.
Rights groups say Trump's administration has provided scant proof that the vessels had anything to do with drug trafficking , warning that the strikes may amount to extrajudicial killings.
Washington has deployed troops, powerful Reaper drones and other military assets to the region.
AFP uncovered at least 20 US military flights to an isolated base on Ecuador 's Pacific coast, including C-130 Hercules and C-17 Globemaster transport planes, V-22 Osprey tiltrotor aircraft and Black Hawk helicopters.
Satellite imagery shows the base undergoing significant construction work in recent months.
The US has also backed anti-narcotic strikes in Colombia , where Hegseth landed on Wednesday.
Washington and Bogota have long counted each other as allies in the war on drugs, with one governing the world's biggest cocaine market and the other its largest producer.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has sought to deepen the relationship even further since his inauguration in August, boosting military cooperation with the US and bombing drug-running guerrillas.
More than 300 US soldiers recently took part in anti-drug-trafficking exercises in the country alongside 400 Colombian soldiers.
Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora, who greeted Hegseth in Bogota, announced the visit on Tuesday along with the delivery of a C-130 military aircraft.
The defense secretary's trip follows an impeachment attempt by Congress that threatened his job less than two years into his tenure.
Analysts say that when the Democratic majority is sworn in in January, Trump's policies and his Latin American alliances will come under fierce examination.

Pete Hegseth says the agreement will include joint training and intelligence sharing with the Venezuelan military.
United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has announced a new agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries.
The Pentagon chief made a surprise visit to the Venezuelan capital of Caracas on Wednesday, becoming the latest in a series of high-level officials under US President Donald Trump to travel to the South American country.
During his stop, Hegseth revealed that the deal would include intelligence sharing and joint training for the two countries’ militaries.
“We see this as a reestablishment of our defence partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries,” he said.
Their shared aim would be “to stabilise Venezuela and rid it of narco-terrorists once and for all”, Hegseth added.
Hegseth was hosted by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who has led the government since her swearing-in on January 5. His trip was not previously announced by the Pentagon.
The Trump administration has exerted heavy influence over Rodriguez and her government after abducting former President Nicolas Maduro during a military attack on January 3.
Rodriguez was previously Venezuela’s vice president. Trump has justified the attack as a law enforcement effort designed to force Maduro to “stand trial on American soil”, charging him with weapons- and drug-related crimes.
After the operation, Trump also said he planned to “run” Venezuela, and he told The Atlantic magazine that Rodriguez could “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro” if she refuses to comply with US demands.
Since then, he has worked with the Venezuelan government to extract concessions on US priorities such as energy development and military cooperation.
Critics have accused the US of reducing Venezuela to a vassal state and exploiting its resources while leaving Maduro’s government largely intact.
Under Maduro, the Venezuelan state was accused of human rights abuses including torture, arbitrary imprisonment and extrajudicial killings.
Still, Trump has held up Venezuela as a model he would like to see replicated in other countries, like Iran and Cuba.
In Wednesday’s remarks, Hegseth said that the South American country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”.
Rodriguez hailed the agreement as a “resumption of the technical-military relationship between both countries”, and she expressed hope that their cooperation could be “brought to its highest possible level”.
Hegseth is also set to meet with officials in Colombia later on Wednesday as part of a trip to the region.
Colombian Defence Minister Jorge Eduardo Mora said on Tuesday that the US would deliver a C-130 Hercules military aircraft, as the US steps up military involvement across Latin America.
Hegseth has faced pressure to step down from his role, following a midterm election in which the US-Israel war on Iran contributed to Republican losses across the country.
A key member of Trump’s cabinet, Hegseth has championed the war, as well as efforts to weaken rules of engagement designed to limit civilian casualties.
Hegseth narrowly avoided a recent impeachment effort in the US Congress this month. The sponsor of that effort, outgoing Republican US Representative Thomas Massie, cited the Iran war as well as a campaign of military strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking vessels off the coast of Latin America.

Hakeem Jeffries is one step closer to making history as the first Black Speaker of the US House of Representatives, after Democrats nominated him for the powerful role despite a small but vocal group of progressive dissenters.
Jeffries, who has served as House minority leader and leader of the House Democratic Caucus since 2023, secured the nod following a closed-door vote. 251 voted for his nomination, compared with 11 against. The move came ahead of a full House vote when the new Congress convenes in January.
Many of those who voted “no” are a group of progressive newcomers, who said in a statement that there is “still work to be done” to ensure their priorities.
Jeffries, who hails from New York, ran unopposed but says he is taking nothing for granted. He faces a restive party eager for a change after voters ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump and his underlings.
Speaking after his nomination was announced, he vowed to "hold the crooks accountable", referring to Democratic plans to reverse Republican policies and investigate controversial moves by the Trump administration.
"We're going to fight to make sure that, in the face of the unprecedented corruption, chaos, and cruelty visited upon the American people, that House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones, because the American people deserve better," Jeffries told reporters.
His fighting talk came after Democrats unveiled plans for wide-ranging investigations into Trump officials and his business interests when they take control of the House in January.
On Wednesday, Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters warning members of Trump's family and senior administration figures to preserve documents ahead of investigations into alleged corruption, immigration abuses and the handling of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Since the midterm elections earlier in November, Democrats, both established and newly-elected, say they’ve been flooded with phone calls and social media posts demanding a fresh start.
Last week, protesters heckled Jeffries during a Democratic conference in Denver, Colorado.
Those opposing Jeffries, including some backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, said conversations are ongoing about his potential new role.
“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they said in a joint statement.
“We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”
He was nominated alongside Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California, who would also be historic firsts, Clark as the first female majority leader and Aguilar as the first Latino to serve as the majority whip. Both also ran unopposed.
The trio will face another vote when the new Congress convenes for the first time on 3 January, 2027.
Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar have risen together, as a team, as the first new generation of leaders of the post-Pelosi era and will likely serve as leaders in the majority for the first time.
When Rep. Nancy Pelosi of California decided to step aside from leadership in 2022 after the party's electoral defeat that handed Republicans the majority, it set the stage for this very era.
Meanwhile, a similar upheaval with Democrats angling for change is happening in the Senate, where Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, a Democrat who’s been the senior United States senator for the state since 2017.

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the Senate also being under Democrats' control.
Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".
As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority. Seven races from the recent midterm elections are still uncalled.
Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.
The Congressional Black Caucus, currently made up of only Democratic House members, noted the potential history-making moment when Jeffries takes the helm of the House.
"The American people, largely driven by turnout among Black communities, particularly across the south, have trusted us to make Washington work for them," said the committee's chair, Yvette Clarke, in a statement. "Now, it is our charge and responsibility to do all we can to deliver on their faith."
Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote , Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.
"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.
All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.
President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.
Trump's opposition could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.
At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".
Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs .
Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.
The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".
Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats plan to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.
Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.
