US President Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin shook hands in China on Wednesday as they were welcomed by their Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping for crucial trilateral talks on Thursday — the first such summit between the leaders of three global powers.
In their first meeting since August 2025, Trump and Putin exchanged greetings and handshakes with Xi, then posed on stage for a family photo at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit gala dinner in Shenzhen.
This was Putin's first appearance in an APEC leaders' family photo in nine years, marking progress for the Kremlin amid Russia's isolation on the world stage following Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.
Xi welcomed Trump at Shenzhen airport earlier on Wednesday, paying particular honour to Trump by greeting him with a hug, reciprocating a gesture the US president made during Xi’s state visit to Washington in September.
When Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their longstanding positive relationship.
Trump said that during the unprecedented trilateral meeting on Thursday he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about ending Russia’s ongoing all-out war in Ukraine, declaring on Tuesday that “I think it’s very close to getting it done".
The three leaders are also expected to discuss trade and nuclear issues as well as the Iran war.
Beijing announced the trilateral meeting as “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the APEC meeting, while Putin said that he expected the summit to be “highly useful”.
Trump has signalled that he wants to take an improvised approach at the APEC summit, betting that his unscripted brand of diplomacy, based on personal relationships, can create a legacy by reshaping world affairs during his final two years in the White House.
Europe and the world will be watching as Trump meets with two of Washington's largest geopolitical rivals after relations with US’ historical allies such as Europe and Canada have turned sour over the last months.
Trump raised the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, which had not yet been confirmed by the time the US president arrived in China.
During his first in-person appearance at an APEC leaders meeting since 2017, Putin met his Chinese counterpart on Wednesday and took aim at what he called “instruments of economic dominance,” such as the sanctions imposed on Russia following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.
“Sanctions, tariffs, and export restrictions” have “outlived their usefulness and have largely lost their intimidating effect,” Putin told a CEO summit on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
He highlighted his country’s desire to cultivate closer economic ties with the Asia-Pacific, saying the region accounts for more than half of its total trade.
In a speech on the sidelines of the APEC summit on Wednesday, the Chinese president told business executives that the Asia-Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth to remain stable and dynamic.
"China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access, but also go a step further. We will carry out reform in challenging areas such as rules, regulation, and standards,” Xi said, reiterating Beijing’s pledges to improve conditions for global investors.
"While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said.
“It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”
Xi and other APEC leaders called for a more open approach, without directly criticising the US shift toward protecting its own markets.
Trump’s “America First” approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC’s aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone, as Washington limits on Chinese access to cutting-edge US technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help to power artificial intelligence, are a constant source of strain with Beijing.
Trump is expected to seek to reinforce the US status as the world’s leading technology power.
His tariffs, intended to curb China's trade surplus, have done little to stop the progress of the world’s dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported $1 trillion more in goods than it imported.
When answering reporters about US policies towards Beijing's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that “we have a very good relationship with China, and you don’t want to insult them.”
Trump’s emphasis on friendly relations with Xi may extend the trade truce reached last year after a series of tariff escalations.
Trump has also said that during his talks with Xi, he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by US companies, but expects Xi to push him on Taiwan’s sovereignty.
“I’m sure he’ll raise it,” Trump said. “I won’t have to raise it.”
The 21 APEC economies account for 60% of global economic activity, half of global trade and 40% of humanity. The leaders will meet behind closed doors on Thursday, while holding other meetings on the event’s sidelines.
APEC does not take binding decisions, but over 37 years it has served as a forum for building a consensus on cooperation and more open trade.
The APEC summit is showcasing Shenzhen, which China has transformed in the past four decades from a fishing village into a skyscraper-studded centre for export manufacturing and technology.

Israeli tanks have advanced towards central Gaza as the military launched what it called a “precise operation” against Hamas, raising fresh tensions over a ceasefire that has been in place since October 2025.
An AFP journalist reported seeing tanks, driven by the Israeli military, position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp, which is located in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza .
The AFP also heard from a security source in Gaza who said there was "intense Israeli artillery shelling" north of the camp and reported Israeli military vehicles in central Gaza "amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes since midday".
The Israeli military confirmed the attack, saying: “The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip.”
The so-called Yellow Line separates Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas in Gaza since an uneasy ceasefire began in October 2025. The Israeli military says it controls more than 60% of the Palestinian territory.
Confirming that the operation involved military and Israeli Security Agency personnel, the IDF said, “there is Hamas infrastructure in the area in the central Gaza Strip.”
COGAT, the Israeli defence ministry body responsible for civilian affairs in the Palestinian territories, has warned international aid organisations not to move through the affected areas.
It said the operation would take place near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps, with traffic also halted along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza's main thoroughfare.
Hamas condemned the operation as a "flagrant violation" of the ceasefire agreement, accusing Israel of failing to honour its commitments.
The Israeli military, meanwhile, said it was responding to apparent violations of the truce by Hamas.
More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, according to an AFP tally based on figures from Gaza's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose data is considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli military has reported seven soldiers and one civilian contractor killed over the same period.

Waymo has taken its driverless taxis off highways across the United States after California temporarily banned the ride-hailing service from its freeways over safety concerns.
The company, a subsidiary of Google’s parent company Alphabet, has "temporarily restricted freeway operations", a spokesperson said in a statement on Tuesday.
As well as California, the pause covers highway rides in the other cities where Waymo offers them, including Phoenix in Arizona, Austin in Texas and Miami in Florida.
The spokesperson said the suspension would allow the company to "evaluate our performance" after the incidents in California, adding that Waymo prioritises safety.
The move is likely to add to the debate over the risks of driverless taxis, which are beginning to expand into Europe.
Waymo has been testing its vehicles in London, United Kingdom, since last year and plans to expand to Munich in Germany and Madrid in Spain in 2027.
One of the incidents went viral last week. A video filmed on Interstate 280 in San Francisco showed a Waymo vehicle approaching at speed and trying to overtake two California Highway Patrol cars. The police cars had their lights flashing to deliberately slow traffic behind a slow-moving construction truck.
The episode led California’s Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), which is responsible for road safety, to temporarily ban Waymo vehicles from the state’s highways from 11 November.
According to the DMV, a separate incident also led to the decision. In that case, "three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure" in the San Francisco Bay Area, an agency spokesperson said.
"Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present," the statement said.
The restrictions "will remain in place until Waymo demonstrates ... it has taken effective corrective actions", it added.
Waymo stressed that no one was injured and no collisions occurred in the construction zone incident.
The company says it completes half a million trips a week. It also says its vehicles are involved in 95 per cent fewer serious crashes than human-driven cars.

The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freeways
Waymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely. The Alphabet subsidiary pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after California banned them from freeways in response to recent traffic incidents.
Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. Those rides remain unaffected by suspended freeway service.
A Waymo spokesperson wrote in an email that the company has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service”, though it’s “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel”. The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they didn’t say how long it would last.
Waymo’s voluntary suspension came the same day as the California department of motor vehicles banned the company’s robotaxis from the state’s freeways. The ban followed two traffic incidents, including one in which three Waymo driverless vehicles drove into a construction zone, a DMV spokesperson, Jonathan Groveman, said in a statement.
The construction zone incident occurred on 5 November, and the second incident, which involved California highway patrol vehicles, occurred the next day on a highway in San Francisco, according to Groveman.
Video of the 6 November incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break.
“The department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” Groveman said.
Groveman added that “similar incidents” previously occurred on 18 May.
The Waymo spokesperson said the “recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California” did not “involve any injuries or collisions”.
California’s restrictions bar Waymo from operating and testing its driverless vehicles on the state’s freeways, according to Groveman. He said the restrictions will remain in effect until “Waymo demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions”.

A Russian national has been arrested in California on suspicion of spying on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defence company that provided support to Ukraine, US officials said on Wednesday.
Igor D'iu faces charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, operating as a foreign agent without notifying US authorities, stalking and fraud.
"Igor D'iu was allegedly recruited, directed, and funded by the Russian government to stalk employees of a major US technology company," Roman Rozhavsky, assistant director of the FBI's Counterintelligence and Espionage Division, said in a statement.
Rozhavsky said D'iu used "physical surveillance, electronic tracking devices, and fraudulent identities to gather intelligence."
US Attorney Craig Missakian said the company was targeted because of its "assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia."
"We will not tolerate any efforts -- by foreign governments or otherwise -- to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations," Missakian said.
According to the indictment, D'iu travelled from Turkey to Mexico in June 2026 before being smuggled into the United States, where he allegedly communicated with his Russia-based co-conspirators via Telegram.
They allegedly instructed him to gather information on company employees and visit a coffee shop near its Palo Alto office to "photograph their laptop screens while they worked."
FBI agents found $18,000 (€15,500) in cash, a fake US passport under the name "Hugo Landry Johns" and two Russian passports during an October raid on D'iu's home in East Palo Alto, according to the Justice Department.
If convicted, D'iu faces up to 10 years in prison for acting as an agent of a foreign government without notifying the US attorney general, five years for conspiracy, five years for stalking and one year for fraud.

Nearly five years after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine turned him into a pariah, Putin is back on the global stage
But Thursday's mini summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping already looks like a win for the Kremlin.
Think back to 2022. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine President Putin was an international pariah. Western leaders were determined to isolate him and his country over the war in Ukraine.
Fast forward to 2026: Vladimir Putin has secured an historic meeting in Shenzhen. For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down – just the three of them – for talks.
That puts Putin exactly where he wants to be: at the top table of global politics, rubbing shoulders with the leaders of the two great powers.
It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.
"We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.
But the Kremlin says the "showstopper" event in Shenzhen will be Putin's trilateral with Xi and Trump.
It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
One short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world. But it's the optics that are key. The picture. The photo-op. Three leaders, three big powers, discussing big issues.
In a way, Vladimir Putin will use this meeting to send a holiday postcard to the rest of the world. Instead of "Wish you were here", he'll sign it: "Look: I'm here."
Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.
Donald Trump has already said that in Shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.
Last month Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting might resemble the Yalta Conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States – Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War Two Europe.
"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.
It is unclear whether China would want the Ukraine war on the agenda in Shenzhen. In its official statements on the upcoming trilateral meeting, Beijing has talked more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
In Shenzhen, Russia will make the most of the optics. But a diplomatic victory is not the same as a military one.
Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.
Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.
And the Ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking Russia to the Crimean Peninsula – carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to Moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.
The damage is not only a logistical headache for the Russian authorities.
It is a reminder that the Kremlin's "special operation" has not gone at all to plan.
The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.
It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami . He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
Federal prosecutors said south Florida was a hub for planning and financing the plot to oust Moïse and install a president of the conspirators’ choosing. The government said Sanon was the conspirators’ initial choice for Moïse’s replacement. Prosecutors also said Sanon helped raise money for the conspiracy and arranged travel to Haiti and lodging for himself and others in that country.
Sanon acknowledged in trial testimony that he was in communication at one point with people trying to replace Moïse, but pointed out that the group had moved on to another candidate long before the assassination. He denied any knowledge of plans to kill Moïse.
Sanon was born in Haiti and moved to the US as a teenager. He testified that he worked with churches in Haitian immigrant communities in Florida and the midwest.
Haiti has not had a president since authorities said that a squad of mostly retired Colombian soldiers killed Moïse and wounded his wife in a night-time raid at their home on 7 July 2021. The poorest country in the Americas , Haiti has a history of dictatorship, political upheaval and foreign intervention that has long hindered democratic rule.
Prosecutors said the scheme to kill Moïse included paying about two dozen foreign mercenaries with money obtained from US government programs that were intended to help businesses during the Covid pandemic, according to court records. US prosecutors have charged more than 40 people with crimes related to the assassination and a dozen have been convicted, including five who are serving life sentences.
The plot to oust Moïse began taking final shape in April 2021, when Sanon met in south Florida with a former Haitian senator and several US businesspeople, according to an indictment. The group agreed that Sanon, once in power, would award contracts to two Florida-based companies – Counter Terrorist Unit Federal Academy and Counter Terrorist Unit Security, collectively known as CTU – for infrastructure projects, security forces and military equipment, according to investigators.
CTU initially hired about 18 Colombian nationals with military training to provide security for Sanon, according to prosecutors. Conspirators also spent months obtaining weapons and body armor and attempting to build ties with Haitian gangs, officials said.
By June 2021, the conspirators realized Sanon had neither the constitutional qualifications nor sufficient popular support to become president. They shifted their support to Wendelle Coq Thélot, a former Haitian supreme court judge who died in January 2025 while a fugitive.
Sanon was previously scheduled to be tried with four other men who were convicted earlier this year, but his case was separated from theirs and delayed for health reasons.

The alleged foreign agent was discovered with two Russian passports
US investigators have arrested a Russian man who they say was recruited by Moscow to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm in California's Silicon Valley that has links to Ukraine.
Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a spying operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco.
He is also accused of stalking employees of the company and possessing falsified identity documents.
The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia. US prosecutors say the company was targeted by Russia due to its assistance to Kyiv.
"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.
"We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations."
Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.
He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".
On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission.
He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there.
His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity".
The suspect allegedly took photos of employees screens at a cafe near the office
According to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, the company in question is Palantir Technologies. Palantir did not reply to a BBC request for comment.
D'iu also allegedly conducted surveillance of employees and their residences.
On 3 September, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days.
During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns".
A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say.
He faces two charges related his alleged work as a foreign agent, one charge of interstate stalking, and one count of fraud related to his identity documents. He faces over 15 years in prison if found guilty.

When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history.
In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.
But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.
"It would be a judgment of landmark importance if The Gambia were to win this case," says Arsalan Suleman, the lawyer leading the case against Myanmar at the court. "It would give renewed vitality to the 1948 Genocide Convention and to the notion of international legal accountability for crimes committed by a state."
The mass expulsion of the Rohingya population of Rakhine State in August and September 2017 was without question a military operation of exceptional brutality.
I was among a very small number of journalists who witnessed the deliberate burning of Rohingya villages in Rakhine, and also the dreadful human suffering of the hundreds of thousands who fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.
Their accounts of killing, torture and mass rape by Burmese soldiers have been thoroughly documented by human rights groups and a United Nations fact-finding mission , external .
I have on many occasions interviewed ethnic Rakhine people about their animosity towards the Muslim population, and I have documented the systematic obliteration of what remained of Rohingya villages by the Myanmar state.
But the question posed at the UN's top court, the ICJ, is whether all of this amounted to genocide.
Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fled across the Myanmar border in 2017 as attacks on them grew
The ICJ was established in 1945 to help settle disputes between states, not to try international crimes. However, it was chosen to address the attacks on Rohingyas in Myanmar because there were few other avenues of redress for the victims.
Myanmar authorities have denied accusations of ethnic cleansing or genocide, saying they were only responding to terrorist actions by Rohingya militants with so-called military "clearance operations".
A UN report in 2018 , based on hundreds of interviews, said the army's tactics were "grossly disproportionate to actual security threats". It said top military figures in Myanmar must be investigated for genocide in Rakhine State and crimes against humanity in other areas. Myanmar rejected the report.
As Myanmar was not a signatory to the International Criminal Court, it was not possible to file a case there against the officials accused of atrocities in Rakhine State.
Instead in November 2019 The Gambia, backed by the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation, filed a case at the ICJ, arguing that all states are bound by the Genocide Convention, so all have an interest in upholding it.
It accused the state in Myanmar, not just the military, of genocide.
This was a novelty in international law; a state not directly affected by an act, arguing that it had legal standing to make a complaint because it was indirectly affected by any violations of such an important convention.
Myanmar objected to this argument, but the ICJ judges ruled that The Gambia was eligible to file the case.
Min Aung Hlaing, the general who now runs Myanmar, was responsible for the military's operations in 2017
The case drew even more attention when the Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, who at the time headed the elected government in Myanmar, chose to lead the initial legal defence of her country at The Hague in person, for which she was widely criticised.
She had very limited influence over the actions of the Myanmar military in Rakhine State, but her refusal to condemn them dismayed many of those who until then had admired her courage and adherence to democratic principles.
Since she was deposed by a coup in 2021 and placed under arrest the defence has been led by a new team appointed by the military.
Historically, proving that genocide has been committed has been very difficult. Judges apply a high bar to this.
Typically, where there is no explicitly genocidal programme, like that of the Nazis, the judges require that the evidence presented at court must be such that the only reasonable inference from the actions of the defendants is that they had genocidal intent.
When Bosnia-Herzegovina filed a genocide case against Serbia at the ICJ in 1993, it took the court 14 years to conclude that while incidents like the 1995 massacre at Srebrenica did amount to genocide, there was not sufficient proof that the state of Serbia had genocidal intent, though it was found to have failed to prevent genocide.
Myanmar's lawyers and Aung San Suu Kyi have argued something similar.
Suu Kyi said that The Gambia's team mischaracterised a complex conflict and military operation, and that while she accepted that war crimes may have been committed against the Rohingyas, that is not proof of genocidal intent.
Aung San Suu Kyi's refusal to condemn the Myanmar military's actions in Rakhine State dismayed her admirers
But Arsalan Suleman believes the weight of evidence his team gathered is enough to meet that high bar.
"What we presented to the court was the long history of discrimination targeting the Rohingya, and how that history, and the policies connected with it, provide a background to understand the government's language, rhetoric, propaganda, and policies that were part of the 2017 'clearance operations'," Suleman said.
"We discussed the 1982 citizenship law, and the tightening noose of discriminatory laws that restricted access to education, healthcare, livelihoods, and travel - all of which made life really impossible for the Rohingya and, we argued, was one of several indicators of genocidal intent."
What happens if the court does find in favour of The Gambia?
Myanmar would then find itself tarnished by having committed "the crime of crimes", as sitting on the same bench as Nazi Germany, the Rwandan Hutu militants and the Bosnian Serbs at Srebrenica.
That might seem a setback for Min Aung Hlaing, the general who now runs Myanmar, who above all was responsible for the military's operations in 2017, and who has been trying to improve his dismal international image in recent months.
There is no right of appeal against an ICJ verdict. However, there is also no penalty that follows an ICJ verdict.
The Burmese coup leader is focused mostly on rebuilding relations with neighbouring Asian countries, who are unlikely to pay too much attention to such a verdict, and much less on rebuilding relations with Western countries who do care.
Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar mark the ninth anniversary of their exodus from Myanmar
But for the huge Rohingya diaspora this verdict matters a great deal.
"This is like formal recognition of our suffering," says Mohammed Nowkim, a Rohingya who was driven out of the Rakhine town of Buthidaung in 2017 and now lives in Canada.
"For the Rohingya, this trial is a moment of acknowledgement of our suffering after years of denial. The Rohingya have been waiting for justice for decades, not just this year."
He and other Rohingya activists hope that a ruling in favour of The Gambia will prompt more co-ordinated action by other countries to find a resolution which allows them to go home to Rakhine State, in safety.
More than a million are stuck in wretched camps in Bangladesh, barred from employment as international funding dries up.
Rakhine State has been ravaged by a conflict between the military and the insurgent Arakan Army, which now controls most of the territory. It is supported by the indigenous Rakhine population who are very hostile to the idea of the Rohingyas coming back.
Many Rohingya villages have been completely destroyed. And international support for them has faded over the years. Even an unprecedented genocide verdict at the world's highest cou…

Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027 . The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.
Only 11 months ago, the EU agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated , the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.
Andrius Kubilius, the EU defence commissioner, said Ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.
The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.
Von der Leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support Ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.
The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.
The EU proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.
The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.
Countries with a triple-A credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the EU budget up to €5bn to expand European borrowing for Ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.
EU officials previously said the UK and other allies needed to do more to support Ukraine in 2027, arguing that the EU was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy said: “The UK, Canada, Japan, and Norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the EU will help even more.”
Britain said on Wednesday night it would send 1,000 long-range attack drones to Ukraine as part of a further £260m military aid package, a day before prime minister Andy Burnham was due to travel to Berlin to co-chair a meeting of Kyiv’s European allies.
The commitment to support Ukraine’s deep strike campaign into Russia emerged a day after the US argued that Kyiv’s attacks on refineries and warehouses were ineffective and counter-productive, earning criticism from the UK and Germany.
“The UK will do everything we can to ensure Ukraine is able to defend itself,” Burnham said.

The president of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, confirmed on Wednesday that his forces had attacked and destroyed the luxurious mansion of one of the main leaders of Haiti's criminal gangs, known as "Jeff" Larose. For now, it is not clear whether the leader was killed in the strike or whether he was even in the house when it was bombed.
Bukele posted a video on the social network X showing images of Jeff posing in front of his mansion, followed by Salvadoran helicopters that approach the building and open fire. The footage shows several columns of smoke rising above the property.
"My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," the president wrote, referring to the 1803 battle that helped secure Haiti's independence from France and make it the world's first black republic.
Thousands of Haitians took to the streets of Port-au-Prince for the second day in a row to celebrate the operation and chant the Salvadoran president's name. "Jeff is a criminal and I hope he is dead. We asked for help and Bukele answered us," said Mario Jean-Pierre, a 45-year-old vendor.
Jeff Larose, also known as Jeff Canaan, Jeff Gwo Lwa or Taliban, leads a gang that has controlled the community of Canaan, north of Port-au-Prince, for years. According to Haiti expert Diego Da Rin of the International Crisis Group, speaking to AP, it is one of the country's most structured criminal organisations and one with the greatest territorial control.
The strike comes after Salvadoran forces also attacked the residence of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, on 8 November. The two leaders were allies and are considered two of the main criminal bosses in the capital.
Bukele deployed about 2,500 troops to Haiti last month , after four Salvadoran soldiers were attacked on 18 October in gang-controlled territory and went missing.
The use of helicopters and explosive drones has made it possible to step up operations against criminal organisations, but it has also increased the risk to the civilian population.
Experts warn that one of the main challenges remains keeping control of the territories that have been retaken and preventing the gangs from taking reprisals against residents.

An Iraqi criminal court has sentenced six French nationals to life in prison for joining the ISIL (ISIS) group, state media reported.
The Karkh Criminal Court delivered the sentencing on Wednesday with representatives from the French embassy in attendance, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported, citing Iraq’s judiciary.
“With these six sentences, the total number of those convicted in this case has reached 16, all of whom are French nationals,” the judiciary said in a statement cited by INA.
All but one of the 16 convicted were sentenced to life. The court sentenced one defendant to 15 years in prison last month.
Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year and charged with belonging to the armed group, which controlled large parts of both countries between 2014 and 2017.
In February, Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries after the United States transferred them from Syria, following years of detention in prisons run by Kurdish-led forces.
For years, Iraqi courts handed down hundreds of execution orders and life sentences to people convicted of “terrorism” offences, including foreign fighters. However, some rights groups denounced the trials as rushed and lacking due process.
Among the foreign fighters sentenced on Wednesday was Thomas Barnouin, a 45-year-old Frenchman, who said during his trial that he travelled to Syria convinced he had a religious duty and did not know ISIL would carry out attacks in France, according to AFP.
The ISIL group swept across Syria and Iraq in 2014, committing massacres and forcing women and girls into sexual slavery.
Iraq, backed by US-led forces, proclaimed victory over the group in 2017, and Kurdish-led forces supported by Washington defeated ISIL in neighbouring Syria two years later.
Iraq is nonetheless still reckoning with the group’s legacy, with mass graves being uncovered and testimonies of its brutality still to be investigated.

Freja, who "didn't expect to be chosen" as the winner, beat more than 1,000 entries from across the UK
A teenage Hunger Games fan has met the cast of the new film after her artwork won a competition, meaning it will be displayed at every cinema screening across the UK.
Freja Brown, 13, won the British Board of Film Classification's (BBFC) create the card competition, which ran ahead of the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping - the sixth film in the franchise.
Freja, from Cardiff, beat more than 1,000 entries from across the UK and said she was "so grateful" to be chosen.
Her design will be the official BBFC black card, which displays the age rating and classification details of the film before every cinema showing.
Freja's winning design will be shown as the official BBFC black card before every UK cinema screening
The Year nine student, whose favourite subject is art, only started oil painting three years ago.
Her mum Marie recalled the moment Freja found out about the competition while scrolling on social media.
"She just squealed and said, 'there's this competition where you can create a piece of art' and she loves making art. So, she was like, 'I'm gonna do it'."
"She's read all the books and watched all the movies, so being able to combine her love for the Hunger Games with her own art sounded really fun."
Freja and her mum attended a fan screening event for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on The Reaping in London
Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace, and Whitney Peak, who play Haymitch, Maysilee, and Lenore Dove in the new film, announced Freja's winning design in a specially recorded video.
Freja said: "I couldn't believe it. I knew that there were lots of other people who had sent in their artwork, so I didn't expect to be chosen and I am so grateful I was."
As part of her prize Freja was also invited to attend a screening of the film in London, where she met some of the stars.
Showing the work to Elle Fanning, who plays Effie Trinket, the actress said: "Oh my God, I thought it was a photo."
Actor Ralph Fiennes said: "It looks wonderful, it's really amazing, I love it."
Freja only started oil painting three years ago, but her mum says she has always been a creative person
Speaking of her inspiration, Freja said: "I was inspired by this specific part in the trailer because it shows the Hunger Games arena to be a beautiful place and not the killing machine that it actually is."
Marie, who is a photographer, said her daughter has always been a creative person and "makes stuff all the time", filling their home with her creations.
Marie said her daughter spent more than a month on the piece and worked until the day of the deadline after she "locked in for a whole weekend" to get it done.
"It's not just a random piece of art somewhere, it's something that her and her friends get to see, which is fantastic."

A court in Iraq on Wednesday sentenced six French citizens, among them the jihadist , to life in prison for belonging to the Islamic State (IS) group.
The six are among 47 French nationals who were transferred from Syria to Iraq last year and charged with membership of the extremist organisation. Their trials began in September. Ten of the group had already been sentenced, most of them to life imprisonment, before Wednesday’s verdicts, which were reported by an AFP journalist in the courtroom.
Barnouin, 45, told the court during his trial this month that he went to Syria because he believed it was his religious duty. He said he had not known that IS would go on to carry out attacks in France.
A convert to Islam in the early 2000s, he was gradually radicalised and became part of a jihadist network in southwestern France. The network included Mohamed Merah, who killed four people, three of them children, at a Jewish school in Toulouse, France, in 2012.
Barnouin joined IS in Syria in 2014. Three years later, Kurdish-led forces captured him.
Iraq’s jails were already holding large numbers of suspected jihadists when, in February, the United States moved more than 5,700 IS detainees from over 60 countries into Iraqi custody. They had spent years in prisons in Syria run by Kurdish-led forces. A court source said their trials would begin on Sunday.
Iraqi courts have issued hundreds of death sentences and life terms over the years to people convicted of terrorism, including foreign fighters. Some human rights groups have criticised the proceedings as hasty and say defendants are denied due process.
At its height, between 2014 and 2017, IS controlled swathes of territory across Iraq and Syria. During that time it carried out massacres and forced women and girls into sexual slavery.
Baghdad declared victory over the group in 2017 with the support of a US-led coalition. Two years later, Kurdish-led forces backed by Washington defeated IS in Syria. Iraq is still dealing with the aftermath: mass graves are still being discovered, and many accounts of IS atrocities have yet to be investigated.
Thousands of Europeans travelled to the Middle East to join IS. France has allowed relatives of French jihadists to come home, but it has refused to repatriate most of the fighters themselves, leaving them to stand trial abroad.

The ICJ is set to decide whether Myanmar's military operations in Rakhine State a decade ago were carried out with the intent to destroy the country's Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) will deliver on Thursday its long-awaited judgment in The Gambia's landmark genocide case against Myanmar, seven years after the case was lodged in The Hague .
The Gambia filed the case with the United Nations' top court in November 2019, formally accusing the Southeast Asian nation of breaking its obligations under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.
In documents and hearings, The Gambia has alleged that Myanmar waged a deliberate campaign of arson, rape and murder in Rakhine State from 2016 to 2017, intending to wipe out the area's ethnic Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.
A UN fact-finding mission later concluded that some 10,000 people likely died in the pogroms. Another 700,000 Rohingya fled the country to neighboring Bangladesh, where most of them still live today in the world's largest refugee settlement.
Even before 2016, the predominantly Muslim Rohingya had been subjected to decades of persecution by the Buddhist-majority country's government, with many forced into resettlement camps and most denied citizenship.
A number of cases over Myanmar's treatment of the Rohingya have been filed in courts around the world. The ICJ will be the first to issue a ruling.
"The Rohingya people have been waiting for justice for decades for the atrocities and crimes committed against [us]. There were no venues available in [Myanmar]… International venues were the only hope," said Aung Kyaw Moe, a prominent Rohingya activist whose family was forced to flee the country during the pogroms.
"We've come over many years to a situation where a judgment will be delivered, and the expectation from the Rohingya community is very high," he said.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
A month after The Gambia lodged its case with the ICJ in 2019, Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, Myanmar's de facto civilian leader at the time, traveled to The Hague to contest the allegations, calling them "incomplete and incorrect."
The move tarnished her international reputation as a human rights icon. Many human rights advocates criticized her for defending the very military that had persecuted her for most of her life.
In 2020, ahead of a final judgment, the ICJ issued emergency "provisional measures" ordering Myanmar to take all steps "within its power" to prevent acts of genocide against the Rohingya, an order rights groups say it has blatantly ignored.
Myanmar's military went on to oust the country's democratically elected government the following year, placing Aung San Suu Kyi under arrest and setting off a bloody civil war that continues to rage.
Myanmar also challenged both the court's jurisdiction over the alleged crimes and The Gambia's right to lodge the case, both of which the ICJ rejected in 2022.
The ICJ then held 14 days of hearings this January for Myanmar and The Gambia to make their arguments before the panel. While Myanmar called one witness, The Gambia called three, as well as an expert.
As The Gambia has accused Myanmar of breaking several articles of the Genocide Convention, Thursday's judgment could be "fairly complicated," said Melanie O'Brien, a professor of international law at the University of Western Australia and past president of the International Association of Genocide Scholars.
The convention outlines that states have a duty to prevent and punish genocide and to establish effective penalties for those found responsible. The ICJ could rule in Myanmar's favor on some of these provisions and against it on others.
"So, there's quite a lot of layers here. They'll be looking at all of those issues, along with, of course, delving into the facts of the case and the individual crimes of genocide and whether or not Myanmar committed those individual crimes with the intent to destroy the Rohingya," O'Brien said.
Proving Myanmar's intent behind the alleged atrocities is the key question the ICJ is grappling with.
Myanmar argues that its actions were strictly part of a legitimate counterinsurgency and counterterrorism operation, and that those actions could not at the same time be judged as acts of genocide.
Days before the Myanmar military launched its heaviest operations in Rakhine, in August 2017, the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, an armed group based in the state, staged a coordinated attack on more than 30 police posts, killing several officers.
The Gambia argues that Myanmar's actions can qualify as both counterinsurgency and genocide at the same time. It also argues that the sexual violence and killing of children that accompanied the operations are proof that genocide was part of the goal.
"It directly undermines Myanmar's argument that this was a legitimate counterterrorism operation," said Michael Becker, an associate professor of international human rights law at Trinity College Dublin and a former associate legal officer at the ICJ.
"Because evidence of those types of atrocities are very hard to square with the idea that this had some other purpose beyond terrorizing the Rohingya population and indeed taking actions to try to destroy them," he said.
O'Brien and Becker said The Gambia's case against Myanmar is a chance for the ICJ to clarify how it weighs such circumstantial or indirect evidence when judging whether genocide has taken place.
Because investigators were denied access to Rakhine State , they had to rely on interviews with victims and witnesses who had fled Myanmar and on reports by the UN and other groups.
"And how the court deals with that, whether the ICJ accepts or rejects The Gambia's view or Myanmar's view of genocidal intent and how you prove it, this will have major repercussions for other cases," said Becker.
The ICJ is grappling with some of the same questions in cases between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, Ukraine and Russia, and South Africa and Israel.
"I'm sure that the parties in the other cases will pick up on what the court rules in this case and add it to their own cases," said O'Brien.
"And even though this case will only be binding on The Gambia and Myanmar, the court itself may also refer to its own law in their future cases," she added.
The ICJ's judgment may have some effect on not only other cases but other courts as well.
The International Criminal Court — which, unlike the ICJ, tries individuals and not states — is considering an arrest warrant request for Myanmar coup leader Min Aung Hlaing in a trial on alleged crimes against humanity committed against the Rohingya. Becker and O'Brien say a finding of genocide by the ICJ could bolster the case for granting the warrant.
What a finding of genocide would actually do for the Rohingya is another key question.
Enforcing any reparations or restitution the court may order would rest with the UN Security Council. But with China and Russia, both allies of Min Aung Hlaing's regime, holding veto power on the council, there are serious doubts about whether it would act on any court order on Myanmar.
Aung Kyaw Moe remains hopeful that the Rohingya will one day receive justice.
"Despite these challenges, there are a lot of hopes that we can [move] toward the betterment of the Rohingya people, including compensation, reparations, transitional justice in the domestic setting in the long term," he said.

İstanbul 'da üniversite öğrencilerinin kaldığı evlerin su faturaları yarı yarıya düşüyor.
İstanbul Su ve Kanalizasyon İdaresi (İSKİ) Genel Kurulu, öğrenci evlerine yüzde 50 su indirimi uygulanmasını öngören teklifi oy birliğiyle kabul etti. İndirimden yararlanmak için ise bazı şartların karşılanması gerekiyor.
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi ( İBB ) Meclisi'nin kasım ayı toplantılarının dördüncü oturumu, Saraçhane'deki belediye binasında yapıldı. Toplantıda gerçekleştirilen İSKİ Genel Kurulu'nda, İSKİ'nin abone hizmetleri tarife yönetmeliğinde değişiklik öngören teklif görüşüldü.
Anadolu Ajansı'nın aktardığına göre teklif, örgün eğitim gören yükseköğrenim öğrencilerinin yaşadığı konut aboneliklerinde su ve atık su bedelinin, konut tarifesinin yüzde 50'si üzerinden uygulanmasını öngörüyor. Teklif yapılan oylamada oy birliğiyle kabul edildi.
İndirimden yararlanmak için şu şartların birlikte sağlanması gerekiyor:
Abonelik sahibinin, konutta yaşayan örgün eğitimdeki yükseköğrenim öğrencilerinden biri olması
Öğrencinin, öğrenci evi olarak bildirilen konutta oturması ve ailesiyle aynı hanede yaşamaması
Öğrencinin konutta oturduğunu kira sözleşmesi, tapu kaydı ya da İSKİ'nin kabul ettiği başka bir belgeyle kanıtlaması
Teklife göre bir üniversiteye ya da yüksek teknoloji enstitüsüne bağlı olmayan meslek yüksekokullarında okuyan öğrenciler bu tarifeden yararlanamayacak.
30 yaşını doldurmuş öğrenciler de indirim kapsamı dışında kalıyor. İndirimden yararlanan bir öğrenci bu süre içinde 30 yaşını doldurursa, indirim hakkı sona erecek.
İndirimin ne zaman uygulanmaya başlanacağı ve başvurunun nasıl yapılacağı henüz açıklanmadı.

Annelik isteğinin ne kadarı insanın kendine ait, ne kadarı ailesinin ve toplumun beklentisi? Kore edebiyatının yükselen isimlerinden Kim Eui-kyung, Merhaba Bebek 'te bu soruyu Seul'deki bir tüp bebek kliniğinin koridorlarından soruyor.
Roman, Göksel Türközü'nün Korece aslından çevirisiyle April Yayınları etiketiyle Türkçede yayımlandı. Biz de kitabın altı çizilecek cümlelerinden 11'ini derledik.
Yaşları, meslekleri, evlilikleri ve banka hesapları birbirine benzemeyen altı kadın aynı klinikte karşılaşıyor. İğneler, hormonlar, embriyo transferleri ve düşüklerle geçen uzun bekleyişte birbirlerine tutunmak için Merhaba Bebek adlı bir sohbet grubu kuruyorlar. Kimseye anlatamadıklarını orada konuşuyorlar: bedenlerini, kocalarını, kaynanalarını, kıskançlıklarını, korkularını. Hatta gerçekten anne olmak isteyip istemediklerini.
Derken grubun en yaşlısı, 15 yıldır tedavi gören 46 yaşındaki Conghyo tedaviyi bıraktığını söyleyip ortadan kayboluyor. Uzun süre haber alınamayan Conghyo'dan Ay Yeni Yılı'nda gelen mesaj grubu sarsıyor: 'Birkaç gün önce doğum yaptım.' Herkesin aklında tek soru var: 'İyi ama nasıl?'
Kara mizahla gerilimi bir araya getiren 160 sayfalık roman; annelik arzusunu, kadın bedenine yüklenen bedeli, evliliği, kariyeri ve kadınlar arasındaki dayanışmayı konu alıyor.
“Tüp bebek tedavisinde kadınların rolü ‘bu haksızlık’ denecek kadar fazlaydı.”
“Acının eşlik ettiği yumurta toplama işleminden farklı olarak sperm toplama işlemine zevk eşlik ediyordu.”
“Muncong’u korkutan şey acı değil, umutla bekleyip hayal kırıklığına uğrama ihtimaliydi yani umut işkencesiydi.”
“Yalnız ölenlerin çoğunun aslında çocuğu varmış, biliyor muydun?”
“Sahip olmak istemek, öylesine sahip olmak istemekti; mutlaka mantıklı bir sebebe bağlamaya gerek yoktu.”
“Bir kolye istemek, bir araba istemek, bir ev istemek gibi, bir de çocuk istiyordu.”
“Ertesi gün, hiçbir şey olmamış gibi karnında ölü bebeğiyle işe gitti, mesaisini tamamladıktan sonra eve dönerken defalarca kaldırımda durup gözyaşlarını sildi.”
“Birisi bana neden çocuk sahibi olmak istediğimi soracak olsa, verecek cevabım yok aslında.”
“Öylesine ‘onu görmek istiyorum’ demekten başka aklıma bir şey gelmiyor.”
“Bir gün kavuşabilirsem gözlerinin içine bakıp ona ‘Merhaba’ demek istiyorum.”

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
İBB Meclisi Kasım ayının toplantılarının 4’üncü bileşimi Meclis 2. Başkan Vekili Gencay Özcan Başkanlığı’nda Saraçhane Yerleşkesinde yapıldı.
İSKİ Genel Müdürü Doç. Dr. Şafak Başa, 2027 yılı bütçesi ve yatırım bütçesini sundu.
Başa, sunumunda İSKİ’nin 2027 yılı bütçesinin 152 milyar 704 milyon olduğunu belirtti.
Sunum sonrası yapılan oylamada ise mali bütçe, 167 kabul ve 47 ret oyu ile oy çokluğu ile kabul edildi.
İstanbul Su ve Kanalizasyon İdaresi (İSKİ) Genel Kurulu'nda, Tüketici Fiyat Endeksi (TÜFE) ile Yurt İçi Üretici Fiyat Endeksi'nin (Yİ-ÜFE) toplanıp ikiye bölünmesiyle çıkan sonuca göre her ay zam yapılması teklifi, 2027 yılında zam oranının yüzde 2'yi geçmemesi şartıyla yapılması kararlaştırıldı. Karar oy çokluğu ile kabul edildi.
Meclis oturumlarında ise öğrenci evlerine yüzde 50 indirimde görüşüldü. “Öğrenci Evlerinde Uygulanacak Su ve Atık Su Bedelleri" başlıklı düzenleme ile üniversite öğrencilerinin barınma maliyetlerini hafifletmeye yönelik su faturası indiriminin kapsamı ve uygulama esasları belirlendi.
Öğrenci evleri için aranacak şartlar ise şunlar:
Abonelik ve İkamet Şartı: Su aboneliğinin, konutta ikamet eden ve örgün eğitim gören yükseköğrenim öğrencilerinden birinin üzerine kayıtlı olması.
Aileden Ayrı Yaşama: Öğrencinin, "öğrenci evi" olarak bildirilen konutta fiilen ikamet etmesi ve ailesiyle aynı hanede yaşamaması şartı aranacak.
Sadece Öğrenci İkameti: İndirim uygulanacak konutta yalnızca yükseköğrenim öğrencilerinin ikamet etmesi gerekecek.
Belgelendirme: Öğrencinin söz konusu konutta ikamet ettiğini kira sözleşmesi, tapu kaydı veya İdarece kabul edilen diğer resmi belgelerle kanıtlaması istenecek.
Tek Abonelik Sınırı: Bir öğrenci, aynı anda yalnızca bir konut aboneliği için bu indirim hakkından yararlanabilecek.
Eğitim Süresiyle Sınırlılık: Uygulama, öğrencinin ilgili yükseköğrenim kurumundaki öğrenim durumunun devam ettiği süreyle sınırlı olacak.
İndirimli tarifeden yararlanan öğrencilerin, öğrenim durumlarının devam ettiğini gösteren güncel öğrenim belgesini her eğitim-öğretim yılında İSKİ'ye ibraz etmesi zorunlu.
Düzenlemede yaş ve okul türüne ilişkin istisnalara da yer verildi. Buna göre; bir üniversite veya yüksek teknoloji enstitüsüne bağlı olmayan meslek yüksekokullarında öğrenim gören öğrenciler ile 30 yaşını doldurmuş öğrenciler indirimli tarifeden yararlanamayacak. Tarifeden faydalanırken 30 yaşını dolduran öğrencilerin de indirim hakkı sona erecek. Maddenin uygulanmasına ilişkin diğer usul ve esasları belirleme yetkisi ise İSKİ Yönetim Kurulu'na ait olacak.
13-18 Ekim 2026 tarihleri arasında İstanbul'da yaşanan yoğun yağıştan etkilenen abonelerin ödenmemiş su faturalarına ödeme kolaylığı sağlanmasına ilişkin teklif görüşüldü. Bu kapsamda, birinci alternatif ödenmemiş faturaların son ödeme tarihlerinin 4 ay süreyle ertelenerek bu süre boyunca gecikme zammı uygulanmaması, ikinci alternatifin ise vade farkı alınmaksızın 6 eşit taksitte tahsil edilmesi teklif edildi.
Öğrencilere indirim ve selden etkilenen vatandaşlar için hazırlanan her iki teklif, mecliste oy birliği ile kabul edildi.

Aile Arasında’nın senaristi Gülse Birsel, ilk filmin ardından hikâyenin bittiğini düşündüğünü söyledi. Birsel, fikrinin birkaç yıl önce bir bayram günü değiştiğini anlattı: Televizyonda kanalları gezerken Aile Arasında’ya denk geldi ve 15 dakika izledikten sonra “Buradan bir hikâye daha çıkabilir” dedi. Not almaya başladığı o gün, 4 Aralık’ta vizyona girecek 2 Aile Arasında’nın ilk adımı oldu.
2017'de vizyona giren Aile Arasında, Engin Günaydın'ın 'Fikret' ve Demet Evgar 'ın 'Solmaz' karakterleriyle yerli komedinin en sevilen filmlerinden biri olmuştu.
T24'e konuşan Birsel, ilk filmi yazarken aklında bir devam filmi olmadığını açıkça söyledi: 'İlk filmi yazarken bu hikâyenin ikincisi olmayacağını düşünüyordum.'
Bunun nedeni ise filmin finalinde bütün kartların açılmasıydı. Birsel'in sözleriyle: 'Bütün sırları ortaya çıkarmıştık, Engin'in karakterinin emniyet müdürü olmadığı, onların gerçek bir aile olmadığı öğrenilmişti. Solmaz'ın aslında bir vokalist olduğunu da herkes öğrenmişti.'
Kısacası anlatılacak bir şey kalmamıştı. 'Hikâyeyi bitirdiğimizi düşünüyordum' diyen Birsel'in fikri ise yıllar sonra beklenmedik bir anda değişti.
Ünlü senarist, o anı şöyle anlattı: 'Birkaç yıl önce bir bayram günü televizyonda kanalları gezerken Aile Arasında'ya denk geldim. Zaten her bayram bütün kanallarda bizim film oynuyor. Oturdum, 15 dakika kadar izledim ve bir anda kafamda bir ışık yandı' diyen Birsel, o an kendi kendine 'Ya buradan bir hikâye daha çıkabilir belki' dediğini söyledi.
2 Aile Arasında'nın ilk adımı da böyle atıldı. Birsel, 'Öyle başladı, oturup not almaya başladım ve iyi ki de almışım' sözleriyle o günkü kararından memnun olduğunu dile getirdi.
Birsel'e göre bazı fikirlerin zamanı sonradan geliyor: 'Bazen daha önce aklınıza gelmeyen bir fikrin zamanı geliyor ve kendinizi ikna ediyorsunuz.'
Üstelik bu ikna sürecinde seyircinin de etkisi büyük. Birsel, 'Biraz da sokakta seyirciden ısrar kıyamet azar yemiş oluyorsunuz' diyerek izleyicilerin devam filmi talebinin ne kadar yoğun olduğunu anlattı. Sözlerini 'Engin de aynı şeyi yaşamış' diye tamamladı.
Engin Günaydın da aynı röportajda kararın Birsel'in 9 yılını aldığını anlatmıştı. Sokakta gördüğü ısrar için de 'Sokakta yaşayamaz hale gelebilirdim. Ondan dolayı ikinciyi yapmak zorunda kaldım' demişti.
Ozan Açıktan'ın yönettiği, senaryosu yine Gülse Birsel'e ait 2 Aile Arasında, 4 Aralık'ta vizyona girecek.

Hilary Swank , 52 yaşında yeni bir bebeğe hamile olmasıyla ilgili eleştirilere yanıt vererek, hayatın ilerleyen dönemlerinde çocuk sahibi olmanın normal olduğunu savundu.
Oscar ödüllü oyuncu, geçtiğimiz ay üçüncü çocuğuna hamile olduğunu doğrulayarak ve eşi Philip Schneider (53) ile ikizleri Ohm ve Aya'yı kucaklarına almalarından üç yıl sonra büyüyen karnını göstererek hayranlarını şaşırtmıştı.
Dün bir televizyon programına katılan Swank, ileri yaşlarda çocuk sahibi olmanın anormal bir durum olmadığını belirterek, insanların çağa ayak uydurması gerektiğini söyledi.
Hollywood yıldızı, 37 yaşında yumurtalarını dondurduktan sonra, 2023 yılında 48 yaşındayken ikizleri Aya ve Ohm'u dünyaya getirmişti.
"Çağa ayak uydurmanın zamanı geldi! Dünyamız çok ilerledi, insanlar çok daha uzun yaşıyor ve birçok kadın daha geç yaşta çocuk sahibi olmak istiyor, bu da oldukça normal bir durum haline geliyor" diyen Swank, "Bana kalırsa, tek bebek taşımak ikizlere göre çok daha kolay, bunu söylemeliyim. İkizlerimle üçüncü trimesterin üçüncü haftasına kadar çalışıyordum, yani çok zordu! Günde 18 saat çalışıyordum ve iki dublörüm vardı, çünkü onlar fazla mesai yapamıyorlardı. Ama hamile, yaşlı kadın yapabiliyordu" ifadesini kullandı.
En İyi Kadın Oyuncu dalında iki Oscar ödülü bulunan yıldız, anne olmadan önce başarılı bir film kariyeri inşa etme fırsatına sahip olduğu için şanslı ve minnettar olduğunu sözleyerek, "Kariyerim dikkatimi vermek istediğim bebeğim gibiydi, dikkatimi dağıtacak şeyler istemiyordum. Ona odaklanmak istiyordum. Şimdi ikisine de sahibim ve kendimi çok şanslı hissediyorum. Çok minnettarım ve her şeyden çok bunu seviyorum" dedi.
Swank, "İki çocuğum var, harika bir kocam var, harika bir ailem var, destek görüyorum. Gerçekten çok şanslıyım ve daha mutlu olamazdım" diye ekledi.
İkizlerinin, aileye yeni bir bebeğin katılması hakkındaki duygularını da paylaşan oyuncu, "Bu bebek için çok heyecanlılar. Sürekli 'Bebek ne zaman gelecek? Bebek ne zaman gelecek?' diye soruyorlar. Ben de 'Noel zamanı' diyorum ve her sabah 'Noel geldi mi?' diye uyanıyorlar" dedi.
Swank, ekim ayında yaptığı bir paylaşımda, "Birçok kişi bir sonraki projemin ne olduğunu soruyor, bu proje aralık ayında yayınlanacak" diyerek üçüncü çocuğunun yolda olduğunu duyurmuştu.

Mert Kara'ya Ertan Saban hayat veriyor. Kurallara bağlı komiser ile alışılmış yöntemlerin dışına çıkan Cevher, karmaşık suçları çözmek için birlikte çalışıyor. Mizahı, gizemi ve duyguyu bir araya getiren dizide Cevher, suçları çözerken kendi geçmişinin sırlarıyla da yüzleşiyor.
Elçin Sangu ve Ertan Saban'a Hasibe Eren, Elit Andaç Çam, Anıl İlter, Sedef Akalın, Berna Cındıl, Alican Altun, Gökçem Çoban, Mert Özen, İlay Karataş ve Rüzgar Eser Düzenli eşlik ediyor.
Cevher, dünya çapında ilgi gören Fransız yapımı High Intellectual Potential dizisinin Türkiye uyarlaması olarak Show TV 'de ekrana gelecek. Yapımcılığını Öner Arslanel üstleniyor, yönetmen koltuğunda Yüksel Aksu oturuyor. Senaryosunu Burcu Yılmaz yazıyor, kreatif yapımcılığı Salih Fahlioğulları üstleniyor.
Dizi , ekrana gelmeden önce hazırlık sürecinde birçok değişiklik yaşamıştı. Kadın başrol için ilk görüşülen Özgü Namal senaryodan memnun kalmayarak projeden çekilmiş, ilk yönetmen Neslihan Yeşilyurt da yaratıcı süreçteki fikir ayrılıkları nedeniyle diziden ayrılmıştı. Ardından görüşmelere başlanan Songül Öden de ekim başında senaryoyla ilgili çekinceleri nedeniyle geri adım atmış, başrolü Elçin Sangu üstlenmişti.
Dizinin kesin yayın tarihi henüz açıklanmadı. Cevher, 'yakında' Show TV'de.

JENNIFER PAK, BYLINE: Well, they're expected to talk about trade, investment, tariffs, which are currently on pause. But I'm waiting on details on a longer-lasting deal, which has so far proven difficult because, well, just take Shenzhen where I'm at here. There are EVs everywhere on the streets. And here at the media center where I'm at, humanoids are serving us coffee and ice cream. I mean, this is what China wants to show off to the world, but look at the latest models of humanoids from China, as well as EVs. They're all blocked or banned from entering the U.S. market on national security grounds. So what's been happening between these leaders' summit is a lot of back and forth. The U.S. has accused China of still restricting the flow of rare earths. These are critical in the production of everything from cellphones to weapons. And then the Trump administration has been adding more Chinese firms and universities on blacklists. So just this week, the U.S. Commerce Department had blocked the remote access of the most advanced U.S. chips, like, from Nvidia, and that will have a huge impact on Chinese AI firms on the cutting edge. MARTÍNEZ: Yeah. Jennifer, the U.S. and China don't agree on a lot. Yet we see Trump and Xi quite warm and friendly with each other. I mean, what do you make of that? PAK: Yeah. I mean, this meeting, like the others, is all about setting a tone. The two sides have agreed to what they call constructive strategic stability. It's quite a mouthful, but essentially what it means is the U.S. and China have agreed they're going to continue to compete but that there should be guardrails. So let's take a look at this Nvidia story. Last week the chief stepped down, and really at the heart of that story are allegations of Chinese espionage and smuggling of high-end U.S. chips to China. JA IAN CHONG: So the good relationship on the surface, but supposedly efforts to get restricted U.S. chips, espionage, all that continues. MARTÍNEZ: And the two leaders, Trump and Xi, will be joined by a third, Russian president Vladimir Putin, for a trilateral meeting. Jennifer, it can't get more different in priorities. So what are we expecting there? PAK: Well, probably more optics, according to Chong. So Trump has talked about bringing up the topic of nuclear arms control. Beijing hasn't been very keen on this because, you know, of the three, it has the smallest nuclear arsenal stock. Senarist ve oyuncu Gülse Birsel, 2017 yılında izleyiciyle buluşan ve başrollerinde Engin Günaydın ile Demet Evgar’ın yer aldığı “Aile Arasında” filminin devam hikâyesinin nasıl ortaya çıktığını anlattı.
T24’e konuşan Birsel, ilk filmi kaleme aldığı dönemde ikinci bir film yapmayı hiç düşünmediğini belirtti. Hikâyenin finalinde karakterlere ilişkin bütün sırların açığa çıktığını hatırlatan ünlü senarist, o dönem anlatılacak başka bir şey kalmadığına inandığını söyledi.
Birsel, ilk filmin ardından neden devam filmi düşünmediğini şu sözlerle açıkladı:
“İlk filmi yazarken bu hikâyenin ikincisi olmayacağını düşünüyordum. Bütün sırları ortaya çıkarmıştık, Engin'in karakterinin emniyet müdürü olmadığı, onların gerçek bir aile olmadığı öğrenilmişti. Solmaz'ın aslında bir vokalist olduğunu da herkes öğrenmişti.”
Birsel’in devam filmi konusundaki düşüncesi, birkaç yıl önce bir bayram günü değişti. Televizyonda kanallar arasında gezinirken “Aile Arasında” filmine denk gelen Birsel, filmi yaklaşık 15 dakika izledikten sonra yeni bir hikâye yazabileceğini fark etti.
O an yaşadığı değişimi anlatan Birsel, “Birkaç yıl önce bir bayram günü televizyonda kanalları gezerken Aile Arasında'ya denk geldim. Zaten her bayram bütün kanallarda bizim film oynuyor. Oturdum, 15 dakika kadar izledim ve bir anda kafamda bir ışık yandı” dedi.
Kendi kendine “Ya buradan bir hikâye daha çıkabilir belki” diye düşündüğünü söyleyen Birsel, hemen not almaya başladığını belirtti. Ünlü senarist, “Öyle başladı, oturup not almaya başladım ve iyi ki de almışım” ifadelerini kullandı.
Birsel, bazı fikirlerin zaman içinde olgunlaştığını ve insanın daha önce düşünmediği bir hikâyeye sonradan ikna olabildiğini dile getirdi. Devam filmi kararında izleyicilerin taleplerinin de etkili olduğunu belirten senarist, “Biraz da sokakta seyirciden ısrar kıyamet azar yemiş oluyorsunuz” diyerek seyircinin beklentisine dikkat çekti.
Engin Günaydın’ın da benzer bir ilgiyle karşılaştığını aktaran Birsel, oyuncunun bu konuda aynı deneyimi yaşadığını söyledi.
Günaydın da aynı röportajda devam filmi kararının alınmasının uzun zaman aldığını belirterek sokaktaki izleyici ilgisini, “Sokakta yaşayamaz hale gelebilirdim. Ondan dolayı ikinciyi yapmak zorunda kaldım” sözleriyle anlatmıştı.
Ozan Açıktan’ın yönetmen koltuğunda oturduğu, senaryosunu yine Gülse Birsel’in kaleme aldığı “2 Aile Arasında”, 4 Aralık’ta sinemaseverlerle buluşacak. İlk filmin sevilen karakterlerinin yeni hikâyesini konu alan yapım, devam filmi için yıllarca bekleyen izleyicilerle buluşmaya hazırlanıyor.

GTA 6 için milyonlarca kişi oyun konsollarının başında bekliyor. Peki Grand Theft Auto (GTA) video oyunu neden nesiller boyunca bu kadar büyük bir heyecan yaratıyor?
GTA 6 adlı video oyununun piyasaya çıkışına birkaç gün kala yayımlanan son fragmanı böyleydi.
Meraklıları oyunu haftalar öncesinden bilgisayarlarına indirdi. Ve nihayet o gün geldi ve Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 kullanıma 19 Kasım'dan itibaren açılıyor.
Oyun konsollarının başına geçen milyonlarca kişi şimdi kriminal çift Jason ve Lucia ile birlikte, şık bir spor arabayla kurgusal ABD metropolü Vice City'de gaza basacak. Oyunun boyutu nedeniyle indirme işlemi, internet bağlantısına bağlı olarak günler sürebiliyor. İnternet sağlayıcıları son günlerde veri trafiğinde belirgin bir artış tespit etti.
Yıllardır eşi benzeri görülmemiş bir heyecanla beklenen GTA 6, şimdiden rekorlar kırıyor. Bugüne kadar hiçbir oyun bu kadar fazla ön sipariş verilmedi. Tahminlere göre yaklaşık on milyon kişi oyunu şimdiden satın aldı. GTA 6, abartısız söylemek gerekirse, küresel çapta bir kültür fenomeni hâline gelmiş durumda.
Oyunda GTA 6'nın kurgusal dünyasının esinlendiği Miami, Vice City'ye dönüşüyor. Miami kenti de bu esinlenmeden mutlu. Hatta NBA takımlarından Miami Heat, "Vice City" adı yazılı özel formalarla sahaya çıktı. Oyunun müziklerinde yer alan sanatçılar Miami'de düzenlenen festivallerde sahne alıyor. Pazarlama kampanyasının bir parçası olan "Vice City" tabelası da yol kenarlarına monte bile edildi.
Oyundan beklentiler büyük. Yaklaşık 5 bin kişi on yılı aşkın bir süre boyunca oyun üzerinde çalıştı. Geliştirme maliyetinin 1,5 milyar ABD dolarından fazla olduğu tahmin ediliyor.
Neu-Ulm Üniversitesi'nde kültür bilimci ve oyun tasarımı ile oyun çalışmaları profesörü olan Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Yalnızca bu rakamlar nedeniyle ve elbette serinin son derece başarılı ve popüler geçmişi sayesinde, en azından çok büyük bir istisnai çıkıştan söz edebiliriz" diyor. Inderst'e göre, çok fazla emek harcanmış bir üründen insanların çok büyük beklentiler içinde olması son derece doğal. GTA 6, günümüzde oyunların oynanış, anlatım, görsellik ve teknik açıdan nelere kadir olduğunu gösterecek.
Video oyunu serisi neredeyse 30 yıldır var ve çıtayı sürekli olarak yükseltti. GTA, siyaset, kültür ve medyayı parodi konusu yapıyor, ABD toplumuna ve "Amerikan Rüyası'na" yönelik acımasız bir hiciv sunuyor. Seri ayrıca oyun özgürlüğünü temsil ediyor.
Oyuncular bu dünyada diledikleri her şeyi yapabiliyor: Bir helikopteri roketatarla düşürmek, berbere gitmek, sahilde yürüyüş yapmak, gece kulüplerini ziyaret etmek, araba yarışlarına katılmak ve daha fazlası.
Oyunla ilgili sıra dışı olan noktalardan biri de kurgusal dünyadaki tüm karakterlerin canlı görünmesi. GTA 6'da bu karakterler oyuncuların davranışlarına şahsına münhasır bir tepki veriyor. Kişiliklerine bağlı olarak örneğin daha korkak ya da daha saldırgan davranıyorlar. Oyunda yaklaşık 600 bin kişi animasyonu var.
GTA 6'nın dünyası yetişkinler için devasa bir oyun parkı. Y kuşağı GTA 3, GTA: Vice City, GTA: San Andreas ve GTA 4 ile büyüdü, Z kuşağı ise GTA 5 ile. Alfa kuşağı aslında GTA 6 için henüz çok genç ancak büyük olasılıkla oyunu yine de oynamanın bir yolunu bulacaklar.
Serinin özellikle GTA 5'in ve çok oyunculu türevi GTA Online'ın kalıcı başarısında, sosyal medyanın da kuşkusuz payı var. Çok sayıda içerik üreticisi oyun oturumlarını Twitch ya da YouTube'da yayınlıyor, özellikle komik oyun sahneleri TikTok'ta paylaşılıyor.
Öte yandan bazı oyuncular GTA dünyasında buluşuyor ve tutarlı biçimde kendilerine belirledikleri canlandırıyor. Örneğin taksi şoförü, yargıç ya da işsiz küçük çaplı suçlu rolüne bürünüyor ve karakterleri için inandırıcı arka plan hikâyeleri uyduruyorlar. Kimileri bunun için bir aksan bile ediniyor.
GTA 6'ya yönelik heyecan yalnızca oyunun kendisine fayda sağlamakla kalmayabilir, daha fazla insanı yeniden konsolların başına çekerek tüm oyun sektörüne de ivme kazandırabilir. Zira Covid-19 salgını sırasında yaşanan yükselişi, stüdyo kapanışları ve işten çıkarmalar izledi. Tahminlere göre, 2022'den bu yana dünya genelinde oyun sektöründen 50 binden fazla kişi işini kaybetti.
Ancak GTA'yı geliştiren stüdyo Rockstar'ın görkemli ürünleri ne kadar ayrıntıya düşkün olsa da hayranların takdir ettiği bu mükemmeliyetçiliğin gölge tarafları da var. Rockstar şirketi, diğer birçok oyun firması gibi, uzun yıllardır çalışma koşulları nedeniyle eleştiri konusu oluyor.
Kültür bilimci Rudolf Thomas Inderst, "Çalışanların içsel motivasyonunun bu kadar güçlü olduğu her yerde, sömürüye başvurmak da cazip hale geliyor" diyor.
Eski geliştiriciler aşırı çalışma saatlerini ve artık sağlıklı olmayan yüksek iş yükünü anlatıyor. Sendikacılar, yönetimin kendilerini gözetim altında tuttuğunu ve çalışmalarını sabote ettiğini öne sürüyor.
Oyunu geliştirenlere şimdi bir sendikanın tanınması için mücadele veriyor. Bu sendika, onlara çalışma saatleri, maaşlar, emeklilik planı ve ebeveyn izni düzenlemeleri gibi konularda söz sahibi olma imkânı sağlayacak. Başarılı olurlarsa bu, adil çalışma koşullarını sağlamakta çoğu zaman hâlâ zorlanan oyun sektörü için güçlü bir sinyal olacak.

Ancak ünlü senaristin içinde televizyona dair küçük bir ümit de var.

Ünlü isim, sektördeki dalgalanmanın beklenmedik bir kapı açabileceğini düşünüyor. Sözleri şöyle: 'Bir şey yazıyorum dijitale. Ama bir yandan da küçük bir ümidim var. Çok saçma; herkesin en ümitsiz olduğu noktada bende bir ümit belirdi. Belki televizyon dizileri bu sallantıda önümüzdeki dönemde kısalır mı diye…'
